title: Scalable Multi-Agent Model-Based Reinforcement Learning
venue: Proceedings of the 21st International Conference on Autonomous Agents and Multiagent Systems
evidence: Closely paraphrased (Sec. 4.2, Results, Flatland): because agents interact, the model "must predict next states of all agents during training"; each agent's latent is linked to the others through a transformer communication block.
method: MAMBA: DreamerV2-style RSSM per agent with discrete latents, coupled by a transformer communication block over agents' latent messages; PPO actor and attention critic trained on 15-step latent rollouts.
evaluation: SMAC (23 maps, 100k-500k steps) and Flatland (5-15 agents), 3 runs; vs MAPPO, QMIX, COMA, QTRAN, G2A, CommNet, 1RL; win rate, e.g. 3s_vs_3z 90% vs 0%; no latency.
contribution: MAMBA scales latent world models to multi-agent RL by letting per-agent recurrent state-space models exchange discrete latent messages through attention, giving large sample-efficiency gains on SMAC and Flatland.
flag: Method evidence only. NO predictive-accuracy metric reported; evidence is win rate/return with baselines and Flatland ablations (L_info, dropout, KL balancing, position encoding - curves only, no numbers). Under the strict v1.6 minimum-evaluation wording this would be E2; recommended include under the Pillar 2 ruling - maintainer to confirm. State is per-agent latents coupled by attention (optionally neighbour-limited in Flatland), not an explicit graph; graph-learning tag is loose. MAMBA loses on bane_vs_bane (39 vs MAPPO 93) and is near zero on 27m_vs_30m and 6h_vs_8z. Flatland results only in figures. Agents need others' latent messages at execution (communication). Generative (observation decoder). Hardware and compute figures not found in the text read. Read via WebFetch summary in one pass.

title: Aligning Credit for Multi-Agent Cooperation via Model-based Counterfactual Imagination
venue: Proceedings of the 23rd International Conference on Autonomous Agents and Multiagent Systems
evidence: Sec. 4.2: "increasing the horizon results in a corresponding increase in prediction error, while CIDE exhibits significantly lower errors compared with DIDE."
method: MACD: Dreamer-V3-style multi-agent RSSM with Transformer communication block and centralized predictors of global state, reward and continuation; counterfactual imagination rollouts give per-agent credit for PPO actors.
evaluation: SMAC (6 maps) and MA-MuJoCo (3 tasks), 5 seeds; baselines MAMBA, MAG, MAPPO, QMIX, HASAC, HATD3, MAT; win rate, return, global-state prediction error vs horizon (256 episodes); no hardware or latency.
contribution: Centralized-imagination multi-agent recurrent world model whose counterfactual rollouts assign credit, with lower multi-step global-state prediction error than a decentralized variant and higher SMAC win rates than MAMBA and MAG.
flag: Predictive accuracy: a DIRECT measure exists but only as a figure (Fig. 5b, global-state prediction error vs imagination horizon 1-10, CIDE vs DIDE ablation, 2-Agent HalfCheetah only, 256 episodes); no numeric error values are stated in the text or any table, and the comparison is against the paper's own ablation, not against MAMBA or MAG world models. All tabulated numbers are downstream (SMAC win rates, e.g. 2s3z 80(15) vs MAG 65(15) vs MAMBA 60(9); MA-MuJoCo returns in curves). If the maintainer requires a stated numeric predictive metric this is exclude-E2; I recommend include on the strength of Fig. 5b plus ablation. No graph structure: state is the joint latent of 2-10 agents with Transformer communication. Training-time model only (imagination for policy learning), no runtime use, no safety content, no latency. Abstract mentions a theoretical proof; proof is in Appendix A, which is not in the extracted text (9-page proceedings version). Std of win rates is large (up to 19 points); 5m_vs_6m MACD 48(19) vs MAG 47(12) is not a real difference.

title: MABL: Bi-Level Latent-Variable World Model for Sample-Efficient Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
venue: Proceedings of the 23rd International Conference on Autonomous Agents and Multiagent Systems
evidence: Closely paraphrased (Sec. 3.1, Bi-Level World Model): the upper-level global latent "encodes information about the global state of the environment relevant to the agent's learning", and the agent latent is conditioned on it.
method: MABL: Dreamer-style sequential VAE with bi-level categorical latents - global latent from environment state, agent latent from local observation; MAPPO trained on imagined latent rollouts, decentralized execution.
evaluation: SMAC (5 maps), Flatland (5 and 10 agents), MAMuJoCo (2 tasks), 3 seeds; vs Dreamer-v2, MAPPO, MAMBA, MAG; win rate, e.g. 3s vs 4z 83% vs 30% (MAG); no latency.
contribution: MABL learns a bi-level latent world model that injects global state during training yet keeps execution decentralized, improving sample efficiency over multi-agent Dreamer-style baselines on SMAC, Flatland and MAMuJoCo.
flag: Method evidence only. NO predictive-accuracy metric reported (no reconstruction or prediction error); evidence is task return and win rate with baselines and ablations (no-global-latent, shared-global-latent, curves only). Under the strict v1.6 minimum-evaluation wording this would be E2; recommended include under the Pillar 2 ruling (method satisfying (b) with experiments) - maintainer to confirm. Text claims of superiority do not hold everywhere: Corridor MAG 55 vs MABL 52, 3s5z vs 3s6z tie with MAMBA at 19, 2s vs 1sc MAPPO 98 vs 92; std very large with 3 seeds. Generative (decoder reconstructs observations). Training hardware RTX A6000/A100; no latency. Read via WebFetch summary in one pass.

title: An Unified Intelligence-Communication Model for Multi-Agent System Part-I: Overview
evidence: "The environment is model as the generic communication channel between agents." (Sec I, brief introduction of the UIC model)
method: Conceptual UIC framework: environment as communication channel, agent as transceiver whose world model acts as source coder; learning agent composed of reactive micro-agents plus representation modules.
evaluation: None. No experiments, simulations, baselines or metrics; case studies (bee colony, multi-robot system) are deferred to Part II.
contribution: A conceptual overview proposing to model multi-agent environments as communication channels and agents as transceivers with an internal world model, without implementation or evaluation.
flag: No evaluation of any kind: no predictive-accuracy measure and no downstream results either. Overview/position paper (Part I of three, a previewed version), so E3 is an equally defensible code; E1 also arguable since no concrete predictive model over multi-agent state is proposed - the world model is only discussed at concept level with reference to LeCun's latent-variable forward model, and the paper says the design is not yet operable in full. Multi-agent state is discussed but not operationalised, so no gap cell is credited.

title: Learning by Abstraction: The Neural State Machine
evidence: "The Neural State Machine is a graph-based network that simulates the computation of a finite automaton" (Sec 3); graph states are kept static once predicted.
method: Neural State Machine: predicts a probabilistic scene graph from an image, then performs 8 steps of instruction-guided attention traversal over it to answer a question.
evaluation: GQA, VQA-CP v2 and new GQA generalisation splits; baselines MAC, BottomUp, LXRT and others; ablations; answer accuracy 63.17 GQA, 45.80 VQA-CP; one Titan X, about 30 h training.
contribution: The Neural State Machine answers visual questions by sequential attention traversal over a static inferred scene graph, reaching 63.17% on GQA and generalising better to held-out content and structure.
flag: Not predictive: the abstract's 'structured world model' is a per-image scene graph that is static once inferred; there is no dynamics, no future-state prediction and no multi-agent state. Falls under the 2026-11-12 ruling (reasoning over a static graph is not predictive for (b)). No measure of world-model predictive accuracy; all results are downstream VQA answer accuracy (GQA 63.17 single, 67.25 ensemble; VQA-CP 45.80; generalisation splits 40.24 content, 55.72 structure), so E2 would also apply under the Pillar 2 rule. Compositional-generalisation splits are the only loosely relevant element (RQ4=2). Default NSM is 63.17 in Table 1 but 62.95 in the ablation table (different split).

title: Learning Latent Process from High-Dimensional Event Sequences via Efficient Sampling
evidence: "The fundamental idea of our methodology is to imitate the event generation process from a bottom-up view" (Sec 2 Model Overview)
method: LANTERN: adversarial imitation learning of a temporal point process; attention-based latent intensity over marker embeddings; next event sampled by random walk on a learned latent relation network.
evaluation: Two synthetic cascade sets, MemeTracker, Weibo (1e5 users); baselines NETRATE, KernelCascade; ablations RNN and heuristic-reward variants; network F1, time MSE, marker accuracy; Tesla K80, no timings.
contribution: LANTERN learns a latent relation graph over up to 100,000 event markers by adversarial imitation and predicts the next event's time and marker, reconstructing diffusion networks with F1 0.57 against 0.44 for NETRATE.
flag: BORDERLINE for (b). It is predictive (next event time and marker) and learns a latent directed graph over markers (users/sites in information cascades), but the authors do not call it a world model and the state is an event history, not a graph state or the joint state of acting agents; multi-agent state is nominal (users in a cascade). Maintainer may prefer exclude-E1. Predictive accuracy IS measured directly (time MSE, marker accuracy) but only in Fig. 3 with no numbers in the text; the tabulated numbers are network-reconstruction precision/recall/F1 (best F1: Syn-Small 0.573, Syn-Large 0.625, MemeTracker 0.423, Weibo 0.566), which measure structure recovery, not forecasting. No downstream task results. Ablations beat the full model in some cells (LANTERN-PR 0.582 on Syn-Small K=5, LANTERN-RNN 0.622 on Syn-Large K=5), so the claimed average 14.9% improvement over baselines is not uniform. Linear scaling claimed without timing figures. The generator is generative by construction.

title: S2RMs: Spatially Structured Recurrent Modules
evidence: "we use a set of M independent RNN modules" (Sec 4, set of interacting RNNs); modules predict future agent-centric observations in StarCraft2 from local views.
method: S2RM: recurrent modules with learned positions on a sphere, interacting by sparse kernel-gated attention; predicts next observations at queried locations from partial local views of several agents.
evaluation: Bouncing-balls crops (OOD ball counts) and StarCraft2 SMAC world modelling (OOD 1s2z, 5s3z); baselines LSTM, RMC, RIMs, oracle TTO; F1, MSE, log-likelihood; single V100 for training, no latency.
contribution: Spatially structured recurrent modules model multi-agent StarCraft2 dynamics from partial local views and degrade least when agents drop out, with out-of-distribution unit-type F1 of 0.75 on 1s2z versus 0.63 for an LSTM.
flag: Reports DIRECT predictive accuracy of the world model (unit-type F1, friendly-marker F1, MSE, log-likelihood, Table 1) with baselines; no policies trained, so no returns or win rates at all. State is the joint state of several agents (per-agent polar images) but NOT a graph; interaction is attention between modules. Gains are mixed: on OOD 5s3z RMC beats S2GRU on unit-type F1 (0.541 vs 0.531) and friendly-marker F1; at 100% active agents baselines and the oracle beat S2RMs (friendly-marker F1 0.763 S2GRU vs 0.795 RMC), S2RMs win only at 20% active (0.642 vs 0.587). Bouncing-ball results are in figures only. No systematic ablation, so the minimum-evaluation requirement rests on baselines. Prediction is in observation space (decoded), not purely latent. RQ4 scored 3 for OOD unit-composition tests, not hazard combinations. Fetched title lacks the S2RMs prefix but is the same paper.

title: Learning Continuous System Dynamics from Irregularly-Sampled Partial Observations
evidence: "In multiagent dynamic system, objects are highly-coupled and related." (Sec 3.1 Encoder)
method: LG-ODE: latent graph ODE in a VAE; GNN encoder infers joint latent initial states of interacting objects from irregular partial observations; GNN ODE function rolls latents forward continuously.
evaluation: Springs, charged particles (5 objects), CMU mocap (31 joints); baselines Latent-ODE, Weight-Decay, Edge-GNN, NRI+RNN; five ablations; interpolation and extrapolation MSE; no hardware or latency reported.
contribution: LG-ODE learns continuous-time latent dynamics over a known interaction graph from irregular, partial observations, cutting extrapolation MSE on springs to 1.78e-2 versus 2.66e-2 for NRI+RNN.
flag: Reports DIRECT predictive accuracy (interpolation and extrapolation MSE, Tables 1-2) with baselines and ablations, no downstream task results. Extrapolation MSE x1e-2 at 40/60/80% observed: springs 1.78/1.81/1.71, charged 6.53/6.43/6.24, motion 1.28/1.24/1.20. Decoder is generative (VAE reconstruction of observations), so non-generative inference is not credited. Graph structure is given, not learned. ODE solver cost (RK4 on a 5x denser grid) is the opposite of low latency; no timing reported. Ablation LG-ODE-fixed PE beats the full model in a few cells (e.g. charged 40% extrapolation 6.45 vs 6.53). Not a safety paper, no interceptor (expected for Pillar 2). Table values taken from a machine reading of the PDF; spot-check before citing.

title: Deep Latent Competition: Learning to Race Using Visual Control Policies in Latent Space
evidence: The approach "combines a joint transition function with opponent viewpoint prediction"; multi-agent world models require "explicit representation of the state and action of each agent" (Sec. 3, Representing Multi-Agent World Models)
method: Deep Latent Competition: multi-agent recurrent state-space model with a joint latent transition over both agents and an observer predicting the opponent's latent; policies trained by imagined self-play.
evaluation: MultiCarRacing-v0 two-car visual racing, simulation; ablations individual vs joint transition vs joint plus observer; win rate 70-80% vs individual after 500 races; no hardware or latency.
contribution: A joint latent world model over two racing agents, with opponent-viewpoint prediction, lets visual policies learn competitive behaviours by imagined self-play and win 70-80% of races against independently modelled agents.
flag: ONLY DOWNSTREAM results: no direct measure of world-model predictive accuracy (no reconstruction, latent or multi-step prediction error); model quality shown only by qualitative imagined rollouts (Figs. 4-5; paper notes predictions diverge after the first turn) and by racing win rates. Recommend E2 per the maintainer's ruling. Criterion (b) itself is clearly met (predictive joint multi-agent latent state). The only numeric result in the text is "70-80%" win rate of both joint methods vs individual transition after 500 races (Fig. 3C); other results are figure-only; joint and joint+observer perform similarly; individual transition is better in single-agent racing. No external baseline, only own ablations. Generative (image decoder). Simulation only; collisions are part of the game, no safety metric.

title: Learning Knowledge Graph-based World Models of Textual Environments
evidence: "The Worldformer is a multi-task world model that simultaneously learns to perform both knowledge graph and valid action generation." (Sec. 4.2)
method: Worldformer: text and graph encoders with two autoregressive decoders predict next-step knowledge-graph difference and valid actions as sets of sequences, multi-task with a Set-of-Sequences loss.
evaluation: JerichoWorld, 27 train and 9 unseen test text games; baselines Rules, Q*BERT, Seq2Seq, GATA-World, CALM; ablations; graph EM 39.15, F1 41.06; action EM 23.22; 4 RTX 2080.
contribution: A transformer world model predicts the next knowledge-graph state as a graph difference together with valid actions in text games, reaching 39.2 graph-level exact match on unseen games against 32.8 for the best baseline.
flag: DIRECT predictive accuracy reported (Table 1, held-out games): next-graph prediction graph-level EM/F1 39.15/41.06 and token-level 51.32/52.45 vs Q*BERT 32.79/35.48 and 53.58/55.74, GATA-W 24.06/25.19, Seq2Seq 14.29/15.54, Rules 4.70/7.25; valid-action EM/F1 23.22/25.54 vs Seq2Seq 18.10/19.44, CALM 13.79/19.11. No downstream agent evaluation at all. Q*BERT is better on token-level metrics (difference not significant, p=0.18). Generative (autoregressive decoding, beam 15, about 380M parameters), so non-generative inference NOT credited. Single agent; the state is a knowledge graph. Possible typo: Table 2 full-model token F1 read as 54.45 vs 52.45 in Table 1 - check. Training cap 96 h per run on 4 GPUs; no inference latency.

title: Factored World Models for Zero-Shot Generalization in Robotic Manipulation
evidence: "We do not learn a mapping from z to s (i.e. the world model only predicts the future within its latent code)" (Sec. III)
method: Factored World Model: per-object CNN encodings with a residual GNN transition conditioned on pick/place actions, trained by single-step contrastive loss; latent-only prediction, ensemble planning.
evaluation: PyBullet UR5 CUBES and SHAPES plus real UR5; baselines RPIN, C-SWM, FWM-AE; five ablations; Hits@1 93-99%, position RMSE 0.5-1.3 cm; one-step search 100 ms per model.
contribution: A contrastively trained, object-factored graph world model predicts purely in latent space and generalizes zero-shot to unseen block structures, keeping Hits@1 above 93% and transferring to a real UR5.
flag: DIRECT predictive accuracy reported (Table II): Hits@1 of predicted next latent 99.4/99.4% CUBES train/zero-shot and 93.2/93.1% SHAPES, and block-position RMSE 1.27/1.05 cm and 0.51/0.68 cm; note RMSE comes from a separately trained MLP probe on the latent and Hits@1 is a ranking proxy, not an error against observed states. Baselines RPIN and C-SWM score 0% Hits@1. Downstream: planning success 95.0/75.0% CUBES and 70.0/67.5% SHAPES with 20-model ensemble (Table III); real robot 40% (12 of 30). Graph is over objects for a single robot, not multi-agent, so multi-agent state not credited. Latency is planning time (about 100 ms one model, about 2 s for 20-model ensemble over 10k actions; multi-step search minutes), far from 15 ms and not a latency constraint, so latency cell not credited. Compute hardware not specified. RQ4 scored 4 for zero-shot compositional generalisation to unseen structures (not hazards).

title: VDFD: Multi-Agent Value Decomposition Framework with Disentangled World Model
evidence: The static branch "has no priors or posteriors, we only use GALA for representation learning" (Sec. 4, Modules of the World Model); action-conditioned branch rolls latents forward with a VAE prior and a graph auto-encoder posterior
method: VDFD: value-decomposition MARL with a three-branch disentangled latent world model (action-conditioned, action-free, static) using VAE priors and GALA graph auto-encoder posteriors; imagined rollouts of horizon 3.
evaluation: SMAC StarCraft II maps (easy, hard, super-hard); baselines VDN, IQL, COMA, QMIX, QTRAN; branch and generative-model ablations; test win rate curves only; no hardware or latency.
contribution: A disentangled latent world model with graph auto-encoder posteriors, added to value-decomposition multi-agent reinforcement learning, raises sample efficiency and win rates on StarCraft Multi-Agent Challenge maps over QMIX-family baselines.
flag: ONLY DOWNSTREAM results: no direct measure of world-model predictive accuracy (no prediction or reconstruction error, no model-loss values); all evidence is SMAC test win rate, shown only in Figs. 3-6 with no numeric values in the text. Recommend E2 per the maintainer's ruling. TITLE DIFFERS: the fetched arXiv version is titled "Leveraging World Model Disentanglement in Value-Based Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning" (Wang and Meger); the method and acronym VDFD match, so I treated it as the same paper under an earlier/later title, not a wrong paper - please confirm. The predictive character is itself weak: losses are KL plus reconstruction of past states/actions, no explicit next-state or reward prediction loss is described. Paper says 21 maps but its breakdown accounts for 16. Loss weights not given.

title: Relational Object-Centric Actor-Critic
evidence: "predicting the next state and reward given the current state-action pair" (Abstract); transition model predicts per-slot change, next state z_t + delta z (Sec. method, Eq. 5)
method: ROCA: SAC-based model-based RL with frozen SLATE object slots treated as a complete graph; GNN transition and reward models predict next slots and reward, used inside the critic.
evaluation: CausalWorld Object Reaching, Shapes2D Navigation 5x5 and 10x10, PushingNoAgent; baselines DreamerV3, OCRL, OC-SA, OC-CA, OCARL; ablations; episode return only; V100 GPUs, no latency.
contribution: A graph-neural-network world model over object slots, embedded in a Soft Actor-Critic critic, improves returns on visual object-manipulation and navigation tasks relative to DreamerV3 and object-centric model-free baselines.
flag: ONLY DOWNSTREAM results: no direct measure of world-model predictive accuracy (transition and reward losses are defined in Eq. 10 but no values are reported); all comparisons are episode returns in figures, plus success rate 0.975 +/- 0.005 (training colours) and 0.850 +/- 0.005 (unseen distractor colours) on Object Reaching (App. J). Recommend E2 per the maintainer's ruling. State is a graph of objects (single agent), not multi-agent, so multi-agent state is not credited. Deterministic world model. Numeric returns are not given in the text. Compute about 13000 CPU-hours and 5000 GPU-hours; no inference latency.

title: A latent linear model for nonlinear coupled oscillators on graphs
evidence: "The goal of LLDM is to model the predictive probability that the system will eventually synchronize" (Sec. III-A)
method: Latent Linear Dynamics Model: nonnegative latent dynamics filters over subgraph phase-difference tensors, learned by supervised matrix factorization, feed logistic regression predicting eventual global synchronization; MCMC motif-sample averaging.
evaluation: Kuramoto, FCA, GHM oscillators on Newman-Watts-Strogatz graphs; baselines concentration rule, logistic regression, FFNN; rank and LLDM-T ablations; classification accuracy 75-94%; no hardware or latency.
contribution: An interpretable latent linear model predicts from short observed dynamics on sampled subgraphs whether coupled oscillators on a graph will synchronize, matching neural baselines at roughly 78-94% accuracy.
flag: DIRECT predictive accuracy reported (Table II subgraph-level accuracy, e.g. LLDM R=8 93.0/94.2/84.8% FCA k=10/20/30, 82.1/78.4/78.4% Kuramoto; FFNN 92.2/95.4/82.8 and 84.2/83.4/79.2), with baselines; no downstream task. Borderline for (b): it predicts a binary long-run outcome (eventual synchronization) from T observed steps, not a step-by-step future state, and it is a supervised classifier rather than a world model used by an agent; the maintainer may judge this E1. LLDM does not beat FFNN/LogReg in most cells. Global-level results are in figures only (Kuramoto peak about 90%). No action, no agent in the control sense (oscillators are coupled nodes). Last 8k characters of the PDF (appendix/references) not read.

title: Bimanual Deformable Bag Manipulation Using a Structure-of-Interest Based Neural Dynamics Model
evidence: "A Graph Neural Network (GNN) then models these particles' dynamics for state prediction" (Sec. IV, Methodology)
method: Action-conditioned GNN dynamics over a particle graph of the bag rim (structure of interest) with handle and rim edge types, used in a constrained random-shooting plus L-BFGS MPC for two arms.
evaluation: Real dual Dobot CR5; bag, collar, hem; model test error CD 1.50, EMD 1.38 cm; servoing success 94.33% vs FEM 78.67%, G-DOOM 72.33%; GNN 0.37 ms, MPC 17.12 ms; RTX 4090.
contribution: A graph neural dynamics model over the opening rim of a deformable bag predicts particle motion under bimanual actions and drives real-time MPC, reaching about 95% success in real shape preservation and servoing.
flag: Direct predictive accuracy IS reported: Table III test-set one-step error CD 1.50 +- 0.16, EMD 1.38 +- 0.17, GD 2.02 +- 0.16 cm, BUT only against loss-function ablations of the same model; the comparison to other dynamics models (MSM, FEM, G-DOOM, visual servoing) is downstream only (Tables IV-VI: preservation 95.33% vs FEM 83.33%; servoing 94.33% vs FEM 78.67%). Maintainer should decide whether a loss ablation satisfies 'baseline or ablation' for the predictive metric; if not, E2. Multi-agent only nominally: two arms under one centralised MPC, graph is object particles, so multi-agent state cell not claimed. Latency cell given because of the per-stage timing table (total about 63.75 ms per command, table sums to about 65 ms; run at 10 FPS) on a desktop RTX 4090, not edge. Paper inconsistencies: text says global sampling beats local but Table II shows the reverse; EMD-only loss has lower EMD (1.37) than the 'best' hybrid. Relies on recoloured rims. MPC distance constraints are planner constraints, not a runtime interceptor.

title: Slot Structured World Models
evidence: "feed the latent GNN-based transition model with an object-centric encoder" (Sec. 1, Introduction)
method: Pretrained Slot Attention encoder gives object slots; an action-conditioned iterative latent GNN transition model predicts per-slot deltas with object-wise L2 loss, no contrastive term.
evaluation: Interactive Spriteworld, 5 objects, 3 test sets by collision difficulty; latent Hits@1 and MRR at 1, 5, 10 steps vs C-SWM; 10-step H@1 68.3-88.0 vs 19.3-23.7; no hardware reported.
contribution: Combining a Slot Attention encoder with a latent graph transition model yields a world model that keeps multi-step latent prediction accurate through chained object collisions where C-SWM degrades.
flag: Direct predictive accuracy IS reported (latent ranking metrics, mean +- std over 4 runs, vs C-SWM): 1-step H@1 98.2/97.5/97.2 vs 72.0/89.7/86.3; 5-step 93.5/86.8/89.0 vs 36.0/50.0/59.3; 10-step 88.0/73.8/68.3 vs 23.7/20.3/19.3 on Test 1/2/3. Caveats: the authors themselves show latent H@1/MRR can mislead (appendix variants reach ~100% latent metrics while pixel predictions diverge), and pixel-space error is qualitative only. C-SWM is perfect on the train set (100 vs 95.7 at 10 steps), attributed to overfitting. Single baseline; toy 2D environment with one controlled agent pushing passive objects, so the graph is an object-interaction graph and multi-agent state is not claimed. Encoder is not trained end-to-end. One-third random and two-thirds human-demonstration data. No hardware or latency. Short workshop-style paper. Compositional/RQ4 score rests only on harder-collision test splits, not unseen combinations.

title: Multi-Hierarchical Surrogate Learning for Structural Dynamical Crash Simulations Using Graph Convolutional Neural Networks
evidence: "Consequently, the fine model only needs to capture inaccuracies and non-captured system behavior of the coarse one." (Sec. 3.4, Transfer Learning)
method: Multi-resolution graph-convolutional autoencoders on simplified FE meshes; an MLP maps time and simulation parameters to a latent state; finer levels learn residuals of frozen coarser surrogates.
evaluation: LS-DYNA kart frame crash, 128 simulations (96 train); mean nodal error vs POD-NN, AE-NN, full-mesh graph AE: 0.49 cm vs 1.57, 0.64, 1.65; prediction 0.05-0.38 ms; Apple M1 Max.
contribution: Hierarchical transfer learning across mesh resolutions lets a graph-convolutional latent surrogate predict crash displacement fields more accurately and over ten times cheaper to train than a single full-mesh graph autoencoder.
flag: BORDERLINE on (b): direct predictive accuracy IS reported (e2 displacement error in cm with baselines: MH1 0.49, MH2 0.49, MH3 0.62, PODNN 1.57, AENN 0.64, GAENN 1.65; prediction time 0.05-0.38 ms vs GAENN 0.91 ms) and the state is a mesh graph (9314 nodes), BUT the model is a parametric surrogate latent = MLP(time, impact speed, angle, yield stress), not an autoregressive or action-conditioned transition model: it predicts the state at a queried time of one scenario family, with no current-state input. Passive structural mechanics, no agents, no control. If 'predictive world model' requires state-to-next-state dynamics the maintainer should exclude-E1. One FE model only; fully connected AE (0.64 cm) is close to the proposed method and faster per prediction (0.04 ms). Sub-ms inference is on a laptop-class M1 Max, not evaluated as edge deployment.

title: Joint-Embedding Masked Autoencoder for Self-supervised Learning of Dynamic Functional Connectivity from the Human Brain
evidence: "reconstructs the latent representation space instead of the input feature space" (Sec. III-D, Context and Target for Reconstruction)
method: JEPA-style pretraining on dynamic brain connectivity graphs: EMA target encoder, block-masked node latents and adjacency reconstructed spatially and from two other time points; GIN encoder.
evaluation: Pretrained on UK Biobank (40,913 subjects); fine-tuned on 8 fMRI datasets; AUROC and MAE vs ST-MAE, ST-DGI, GraphMAE etc.; e.g. ABIDE diagnosis AUROC 71.49 vs 69.73; RTX A6000.
contribution: A joint-embedding masked autoencoder for dynamic functional-connectivity graphs that reconstructs masked node latents across space and time and improves downstream fMRI phenotype prediction over generative pretraining.
flag: ONLY DOWNSTREAM RESULTS: no metric of latent-prediction accuracy at all; every number is downstream gender AUROC, age MAE, diagnosis AUROC, linear probing, multi-task or ablation scores. Hence exclude-E2 per ruling. Predictiveness is also doubtful: the graph IS dynamic (sliding-window connectivity), so the static-graph ruling does not apply literally, but the temporal objective is interpolation - masked latents at time t are predicted from context at t_a BEFORE and t_b AFTER t - not forecasting of future state, and there is no dynamics/transition model or actions. Maintainer may prefer exclude-E1 on that ground. Single-subject brain graphs, not agents. Figures 2-5 values not extractable; ST-JEMA ADHD200 multi-task row missing from my read. Last ~7k characters not read (likely references).

title: Planning with Adaptive World Models for Autonomous Driving
evidence: "BehaviorNet predicts the parameters of an agent's motion controller rather than directly predicting its spacetime trajectory" (Abstract)
method: MPC planner (extends PDM-C) scoring proposals in a rule-based reactive world model; a LaneGCN-style graph network predicts per-city or per-log IDM parameters for surrounding agents.
evaluation: nuPlan closed-loop Val-14 and Test-14 Hard vs PDM-C, PlanTF, PlanAgent etc.; R-CLS 93.49 and 78.87 (PDM-C 91.79, 75.18); 249 ms vs 232 ms on RTX 3090.
contribution: Adapting the IDM parameters of a rule-based traffic world model to each scene with a graph network improves closed-loop nuPlan planning scores over PDM-C at about 17 ms extra latency.
flag: ONLY DOWNSTREAM RESULTS: no direct measure of world-model predictive accuracy (no ADE/FDE, no parameter-fit error reported); evidence is closed-loop NR-CLS/R-CLS, an oracle-vs-predicted IDM gap in planning score (Table IV, -0.07 to -0.14) and qualitative figures. Hence exclude-E2 per ruling. Also weak on (b): the world model is rule-based IDM (not learned, not latent), the network predicts controller parameters, one parameter set per city or log cluster (K=16), and IDM interacts only with the lead vehicle, so E1 is also arguable. No collision rate, only composite scores. Baseline numbers copied from prior work. Text says gains 'up to 1.74%' but Table III LAS shows 97.25 vs 95.21 (2.04). Latency 249 ms is planner-level, far from sub-15 ms.

title: Modeling the Real World with High-Density Visual Particle Dynamics
evidence: "HD-VPD is a 3D dynamics model disguised as a video prediction model." (Sec. 2, HD-VPD: High-density visual particle dynamics world models)
method: Action-conditioned particle world model: RGB-D encoded to 3D latent particles; Interlacer transformer alternates kNN neighbour attention and linear-attention Performer layers; point-NeRF renderer; pixel L2 rollouts.
evaluation: Real bimanual KUKA iiwa data (~60 tasks, 5 cells); SSIM and speed vs hierarchical GNN (VPD) and Performer-PCT across particle counts up to 131K; values in figures only; GPU unstated.
contribution: A deterministic particle-based world model for real bimanual robots whose Interlacer transformer scales latent 3D dynamics to over 100K particles, matching GNN prediction quality at about twice the speed.
flag: BORDERLINE on (b) state type: the state is a particle set for ONE bimanual robot scene; graph structure exists only as kNN neighbourhoods (s=16) in the Neighbor-Attender layers, and the proposed model is pitched as a transformer replacing the GNN. Not multi-agent (two arms under one controller). If the maintainer reads 'graph state' strictly this is E1. Direct predictive measure IS reported (test-set SSIM of rendered rollouts vs GNN and Performer-PCT baselines, by particle count and rollout horizon) but ONLY in figures (Fig. 5a, Fig. 6); no numeric SSIM in the text, so no value could be extracted. Speed claims (2x faster, 4x particles than GNN) also figure-only; no absolute latency or GPU model. Planning results (box push, grasp cost) are qualitative, no success rates.

title: Learning Networked Dynamical System Models with Weak Form and Graph Neural Networks
evidence: "The wGKBF model extends the wLDM framework by employing GCLs in the encoder and decoder" (Sec. IV.C, Weak Graph Koopman Bilinear Form)
method: Latent dynamics models trained with a weak-form residual; graph variant (wGKBF) uses Chebyshev graph-conv encoder/decoder and a bilinear Koopman latent processor with control inputs.
evaluation: Simulated double pendulum, Brusselator, 24-state aircraft energy network; NRMSE vs NODE, LSTM, biDMDc; wGKBF 3.38E-2 vs biDMDc 5.82E-1; RTX 3090, training times only.
contribution: Weak-form training of control-conditioned latent dynamics, extended to networked systems with a graph Koopman bilinear model that cuts trajectory NRMSE by an order of magnitude against bilinear DMD on a 24-state aircraft energy network.
flag: Direct predictive accuracy IS reported (trajectory NRMSE with baselines): pendulum wLDM 9.41E-4 vs NODE 1.11E-3 vs LSTM 2.28E-2; Brusselator 0.003-0.013 vs NODE 0.011-0.159; aircraft wGKBF mean 3.38E-2 vs biDMDc 5.82E-1. Only the third experiment is on a graph (one engineered network of 24 states, 3 inputs, a component graph, not agents); the first two are non-graph ODEs. All data simulated. No inference latency, only training time (wGKBF 16680 s vs biDMDc 724 s, i.e. slower to train). Graph NODE baseline was not run (cost). Table 5 min and max columns look swapped. Control use (MPC) is future work. I did not read the last ~10k characters (likely references/appendix).

title: Deliberate Reasoning in Language Models as Structure-Aware Planning with an Accurate World Model
evidence: "SWAP leverages entailment graphs to encode structured dependencies and enable symbolic verification of intermediate steps." (Abstract)
method: LLM reasoning as planning: a fine-tuned LM world model predicts the next reasoning state and entailment graph, symbolic checks filter candidates, a discriminator ranks them in breadth-limited search.
evaluation: GSM8K, MATH500, FOLIO, ReClor, HumanEval, MBPP with LLaMA3-8B and Mistral-7B; vs CoT, self-consistency, ToT, RAP, PRM; LLaMA3 accuracy 92.6, 43.2, 79.2, 78.1, 68.8, 68.0; 12.4k tokens; no hardware or latency.
contribution: Frames LLM multi-step reasoning as planning with a learned world model that predicts next states and an entailment graph, verified symbolically and ranked by a discriminator, improving reasoning accuracy.
flag: No direct measure of next-state prediction accuracy of the world model; evidence is task accuracy and ablations (w/o state-prediction refinement 88.0 vs 92.6 on GSM8K; w/o planning 80.1/32.0; w/o SFT 87.8/31.2). Borderline: a manual check of constructed entailment graphs on 100 FOLIO samples (node accuracy 90.0, graph accuracy 68.0 vs SFT-CoT 81.8/52.0) is a quasi-direct measure of the predicted graph against a baseline - if the maintainer accepts that, this could be include; I recommend exclude-E2 because it scores the final graph, not the world model's predictions. (b) is nominal: the graph is an entailment graph over reasoning statements in a single LLM system, not multi-agent or environment state, so E1 is also defensible. Symbolic verification discards invalid candidate states during search, which is internal to the planner and not a runtime interceptor on an acting system. Last ~40k characters (appendices) not read.

title: FACTS: A Factored State-Space Framework For World Modelling
evidence: "we conceptualise the hidden state Z_t as a graph and hence, the state-space memory is represented as a set of nodes" (Sec. 3.1)
method: Recurrent factored state-space model: memory is a set of latent factor nodes updated through attention routing from input feature nodes, permutation-invariant to inputs, with latent future prediction.
evaluation: 9 multivariate forecasting sets, CLEVRER/OBJ3D slot dynamics, METR-LA (207 sensors); vs iTransformer, S-Mamba, SlotFormer, TESTAM; METR-LA RMSE 6.97, MAE 3.11, MAPE 9.08%; single A100; no latency.
contribution: A factored state-space world model whose graph-structured latent memory is routed by attention and is permutation-robust, evaluated on time-series forecasting, object-centric dynamics and traffic-graph prediction.
flag: Direct predictive accuracy IS reported with baselines: forecasting MSE/MAE on 9 datasets (e.g. ETTm1 0.392/0.397, Electricity 0.166/0.263, Traffic 0.472/0.303), LPIPS 0.09 CLEVRER and 0.07 OBJ3D vs SlotFormer 0.11/0.08, METR-LA 6.97/3.11/9.08% vs TESTAM 7.09/3.36/9.67%. Doubts: 'graph or multi-agent state' holds only loosely - the latent factors form a learned bipartite routing graph and the 'agents' are sensors, variates or object slots; the gap cell multi-agent state is generous and maintainer may strike it or call the paper generic time-series forecasting (E1). Paper claims best on 6 of 9 forecasting sets but is beaten on Traffic by S-Mamba 0.414 and iTransformer 0.428. Forecasting is single-step encoder-style, not autoregressive rollout. Routing uses Z_0 not Z_t-1 for parallelism. Last ~17k characters of appendix (rest of ablations) were not read. No safety content, no interceptor.

title: SPARTAN: A Sparse Transformer World Model Attending to What Matters
evidence: "SPARTAN learns sparse, context-dependent interaction graphs that accurately predict future object states." (Abstract)
method: Transformer world model over per-entity tokens that samples a sparse state-dependent adjacency (Gumbel-softmax attention mask) as a local causal graph and predicts next-step entity states.
evaluation: Interventional Pong, CREATE, Waymo traffic; vs dense Transformer, Global Graph, MTR; prediction error 8.60/246.6/0.52, SHD 1.51/1.17/6.84 (Transformer 6.37/6.29/10.6); V100/RTX 6000 training; no latency.
contribution: A sparse-attention Transformer world model that learns state-dependent interaction graphs among entities while predicting their future states, improving graph recovery and robustness to irrelevant entities.
flag: Direct predictive accuracy IS reported with baselines (Table 1 prediction error and structural Hamming distance; Table 2 robustness when non-causal entities are removed: 24.5/28.6/13.9% vs Transformer 1140.2/138.2/32.8%). Caveats: prediction error is about equal to the dense Transformer (Traffic 0.52 vs 0.51, slightly worse; learned-slot Pong 7.21 vs 6.90, worse) - the gain is sparsity and robustness, not accuracy; units of error not stated; few-shot adaptation results are in Fig. 4 only; CoDA is named as a baseline but no numbers appear. Multi-agent only in the Waymo setting (ego prediction, about 50 vehicles); Pong and CREATE are object-centric. Simulated domains use ground-truth masks. RQ4 score reflects unseen combinations of interventions, not hazards. No safety content, no interceptor.

title: Predict, Cluster, Refine: A Joint Embedding Predictive Self-Supervised Framework for Graph Representation Learning
evidence: "The objective is computed at the latent space with no reconstruction/negative sampling involved." (Sec. 3.2.1)
method: JEPA-style graph self-supervision: a context encoder on a node-masked subgraph predicts EMA-target embeddings of three masked target subgraphs, plus a GMM/k-means pseudo-label consistency loss.
evaluation: Node classification by linear evaluation on 7 static graphs (Cora 89.8, Citeseer 77.0, Pubmed 85.7, Photos 94.5, Computers 88.0, CS 94.5, WikiCS 82.4) vs DGI, BGRL, GraphMAE etc.; M2 MacBook; no latency.
contribution: Joint-embedding predictive self-supervised learning on static graphs, predicting masked subgraph embeddings in latent space with a clustering-based pseudo-label term, evaluated on node classification.
flag: Static-graph masked/multi-view latent prediction with no future state or dynamics: exclude-E1 under the 2026-11-12 ruling. No direct predictive-accuracy measure, only downstream node-classification accuracy (so E2 would also apply). Title on the fetched arXiv version is "Leveraging Joint Predictive Embedding and Bayesian Inference in Graph Self Supervised Learning", not the record title; content (JEPA predictor plus clustering refinement) matches, so I treated it as another version of the same paper, not a wrong paper - maintainer should confirm. Paper is internally inconsistent on encoder widths and number of predictors; baseline scores are copied from other papers.

title: Free Energy Risk Metrics for Systemically Safe AI: Gatekeeping Multi-Agent Study
evidence: "toggle their vehicle's policy to Defensive in risky situations, or back to Hotshot when deemed safe enough" (Sec. 3.4)
method: Gatekeepers score an agent's policy by a free-energy Cumulative Risk Exposure from Monte Carlo rollouts, average risk over neighbouring gatekeepers, and switch the vehicle to a defensive policy above threshold.
evaluation: highway-env, 24 vehicles (12 ego, 12 alter), 1200 runs x 80 steps; baselines all-Defensive and all-Hotshot vs 4 or 12 gatekept egos; loss and cumulative crashes in Fig. 1 only; no hardware or latency.
contribution: Proposes a free-energy risk metric with which per-vehicle gatekeepers, sharing risk with neighbours, switch driving policies at runtime; simulated highway traffic gets safer as more vehicles are gatekept.
flag: Under Pillar 2 (b) this would fail: there is no learned world model (the gatekeeper rolls out the fully observable simulator, 128 trajectories, horizon 10) and NO direct predictive-accuracy measure; entropic terms are dropped so the risk is time-discounted expected utility. I recommend include on (a)/(c) instead, as a runtime gatekeeper with crash counts against two baselines - maintainer should confirm this record may be judged on (a). Weak evaluation: all results are in Fig. 1 (90% CIs) and prose, no table or numeric values; only stated figure is 10-40% of egos in Defensive mode; reward constants not given; no ablation of thresholds, horizon or neighbour averaging. The gatekeeper switches a whole policy, it does not veto single actions. (c) primacy is arguable. Quotes obtained via a PDF reader summary; verify wording.

title: A Social Dynamical System for Twitter Analysis
evidence: "Experimental results confirm the effectiveness of LSDS." (Sec. 1, Introduction)
method: LSDS: temporal-graph encoder maps each account's tweet embeddings to a latent opinion state; a GNN-based GraphODE rolls latent states forward over the follower graph; decoders predict interactions and polarity.
evaluation: 513 politicians plus 287 others, 2020 weekly, 50 sequences, first half observed and second half predicted; encoder and ODE variants incl. No-Update; ROC-AUC, MSE, accuracy, R2; RTX A4000, 20-30 s per epoch.
contribution: A latent graph-ODE model of opinion dynamics on a Twitter follower network predicts future interactions with 0.912 ROC-AUC and future polarity with 0.177 MSE from the first half of each sequence.
flag: Predictive accuracy: DIRECT measures on held-out future steps are reported (interaction ROC-AUC 0.9119, PR-AUC 0.8997; polarity MSE 0.1770, MAPE 1.7894; classification acc 0.8925; embedding MSE 0.0097, R2 0.4281; 5 seeds). Doubts: the gain from dynamics is marginal - the No-Update ablation (opinions held constant) gets ROC-AUC 0.8950 and polarity MSE 0.1741, BETTER than the default on MSE, and DeGroot and BCM also beat it on MSE (0.1731); the authors concede limited opinion fluctuation. Evidence that encoder choice matters far more than the ODE. Polarity labels come from a pretrained embedding model, not human annotation; no external published baseline, only internal variants; one dataset; the follower graph is static, only node states evolve; an embedding-reconstruction decoder exists, so non-generative inference is arguable - check. Domain is social media analysis, no control, safety or latency aspect. Only training time per epoch given, no inference latency. Evidence quote is weak; longer-horizon results are figures only. New tag neural-ode added.

title: AI in a vat: Fundamental limits of efficient world modelling for agent sandboxing and interpretability
evidence: "we identify a fundamental trade-off between the computational efficiency of a world model and its interpretability" (Sec. 1, Introduction)
method: Theory of world models as transducers (POMDPs as a special case) for sandboxing and interpreting an AI agent; proves minimality, reduction and reversibility results.
evaluation: No experiments: theorems only (epsilon-transducer minimality, generalised transducer reduction, reversibility conditions) and one illustrative card-deck example; no baselines, metrics, hardware or latency.
contribution: Formalises world models as transducers and proves a fundamental trade-off between a world model's computational efficiency and its interpretability, with minimality results for predictive models.
flag: Predictive accuracy: NONE, neither direct nor downstream - purely theoretical, correctness by exact equivalence proofs. Recommend E1 because the world model has no graph or multi-agent state: single agent-environment interface, agent-agnostic; graphical models appear only to depict factorisation. A formal result can satisfy the evaluation requirement, so E2 is not the main ground, but if the maintainer reads the state requirement loosely it would still fail the v1.6 predictive-accuracy minimum. Sandboxing here means offline construction of a simulated world for evaluating an agent, not a runtime interceptor. Last 14k characters (appendix end) not read.

title: SocioVerse: A World Model for Social Simulation Powered by LLM Agents and A Pool of 10 Million Real-World Users
evidence: "SocioVerse can reflect large-scale population dynamics" (Abstract)
method: Social simulation pipeline: 10M real user profiles, demographic sampling (IPF or IDS), LLM persona agents answer questionnaires; aggregate answers compared with real outcomes.
evaluation: US election (331,836 agents), breaking news (20,000), China economic survey (16,000); five to six LLMs compared, knowledge and prior ablations; accuracy, RMSE, KL, NRMSE; 8 RTX 4090; no latency.
contribution: LLM persona agents sampled from a 10-million-user pool reproduce US state election outcomes with up to 0.922 accuracy and 0.037 RMSE, and regional spending distributions with KL as low as 0.016.
flag: Predictive accuracy: DIRECT measures against real outcomes are reported (election accuracy up to 0.922, RMSE 0.037; battleground up to 0.867; economic KL 0.016-0.066; Table 4 ablation), so this is not E2. Recommend E1 because, on reading, it is not a predictive world model over joint multi-agent state: it is a prompting and sampling pipeline in which agents answer survey questions independently, no state transition or dynamics is learned or predicted, the interaction scenario is described but NOT evaluated, and the comparisons are retrospective (outcomes may be in LLM training data). World model is used in the title only nominally. If the maintainer treats population-level outcome prediction from many agents as (b), it would be includable with multi-agent state. Caveats: Table 3 column headers were garbled in extraction so per-model values may be misassigned, and the text's claim on which model is best on the news task did not match the values as I read them; news-task ground truth is itself LLM-derived; no external baseline system. New tag social-simulation added.

title: WALL-E 2.0: World Alignment by NeuroSymbolic Learning improves World Model-based LLM Agents
evidence: "Our LLM-based MPC framework overcomes the inefficiency of classical MPC that requires online k-step optimization" (Sec. 1, Introduction)
method: LLM world model aligned with learned code rules, a knowledge graph and a scene graph; inside an MPC loop it predicts success or failure of a proposed action and forces replanning.
evaluation: Mars (Crafter-based, 8 world types) and ALFWorld (134 tasks); vs PPO, DreamerV3, ReAct, Reflexion, IfR, WALL-E 1.0; reward, score, success, rule cover rate; ablations; no hardware or latency.
contribution: A neurosymbolic LLM world model whose learned code rules and scene graph check each proposed action before execution, reaching 98% ALFWorld success and Mars reward 6.7 and score 15.3% against 5.5 and 7.4% for IfR.
flag: BORDERLINE, maintainer should decide. Predictive accuracy: NO overall accuracy of the world model is reported; the only direct measure is cover rate (share of the LLM's mispredicted transitions corrected by learned rules, 0.0% to 92.3% over iterations, Fig. 6), everything else is downstream (Mars reward 6.7 and score 15.3%, ALFWorld 98%). If cover rate is not accepted as a predictive-accuracy metric this is exclude-E2 under the maintainer's practice. Graph state is also weak: SINGLE agent; the scene graph and knowledge graph supplement a textual/JSON observation, and the model predicts a binary success flag rather than next graph state - could be E1. runtime_interceptor yes because the world model rejects a proposed action before execution and triggers replanning, but this is task-feasibility checking inside the planner, not a safety mechanism, so (a) not claimed and no safety metric. Abstract numbers inconsistent with body: abstract says reward gains 16.1-51.6% and score at least 61.7%, body text says score exceeds IfR by 51.6%. DreamerV3 has higher average reward (7.9) than WALL-E 2.0 (6.7). ReplanLimit value not found; no LLM call latency. Marked preliminary work. Last 10k characters not read. New tag neurosymbolic added.

title: Hurdle Network Model With Latent Dynamic Shrinkage For Enhanced Edge Prediction in Zero-Inflated Directed Network Time Series
evidence: "Hurdle-Net(1) performs comparably to the independent model in terms of nonzero trade volume prediction" (Sec. 5, Bilateral Trade Flows)
method: Bayesian hurdle model for zero-inflated directed network time series: node latent positions evolve under a dynamic shrinkage prior and jointly drive edge occurrence and edge weight; HMC inference.
evaluation: Simulations (5-20 nodes, T=11, predict t=11) and apparel trade among 29 countries (train 1994-2012, test 2013); vs independent, static and d=0 variants; LOO-IC, out-of-sample error; no hardware.
contribution: A Bayesian latent-position model with dynamic shrinkage predicts next-step edge occurrence and weight in sparse directed network time series, improving held-out trade-occurrence error by about 66% over an independent-latent baseline.
flag: Predictive accuracy: DIRECT measure reported (out-of-sample edge-occurrence and weight error at a held-out time point, LOO-IC), no downstream task at all; but the values are in figures only (Figs. 3-9), the only number in the text is the about 66% improvement in trade-occurrence error over the independent model; weight prediction is only comparable. Doubts: this is a statistics/econometrics paper (international trade), nodes are countries not acting agents, no control, safety or real-time aspect - meets (b) only as latent dynamic prediction over a time-varying graph, maintainer may judge it E1 on scope; one-step-ahead only; how latent positions are extrapolated to the test time is not spelled out; HMC inference, no runtime or hardware reported; largest network 29 nodes. New tag bayesian-inference added. Gap cell multi-agent state not claimed (graph nodes are not agents).

title: Causal Cartographer: From Mapping to Reasoning Over Counterfactual Worlds
evidence: "we rely on human sources and only use the LLM agent to perform causal extraction" (Sec. 3.1, closely quoted)
method: LLM agent extracts a causal knowledge graph (CausalWorld, 975 nodes, 1337 edges) from 2020 news; a second ReAct-style agent answers counterfactual queries stepwise over that static graph.
evaluation: CausalWorld-CR, 400 observational and counterfactual queries; o3-mini, GPT-4.1, LLaMA-3.1-8B vs CausalCoT; accuracy, relative error, BLEU, tokens (figures only); 8 A100; no latency.
contribution: Builds a causal graph of real-world events from news and an LLM agent that answers counterfactual queries over it step by step, cutting LLaMA-3.1-8B context by 72% versus causal chain-of-thought.
flag: Predictive accuracy: a direct answer-accuracy and relative-error measure exists but only as figures (Fig. 7), no numeric values found in the text; authors say accuracy is only slightly better than or similar to CausalCoT. Recommend E1 under the 2026-11-12 ruling: the graph is a STATIC causal graph, inference is counterfactual (abduction-intervention-prediction), there is no dynamics model and no prediction of future state; single LLM agent, not multi-agent. If the maintainer counts counterfactual inference over a graph as predictive, this becomes borderline (b). Abstract claim of inference cost cut up to 70%: body gives 72% context and 91% output reduction for LLaMA-3.1-8B only. No ablation. New tag causal-inference added.

title: Ego-centric Learning of Communicative World Models for Autonomous Driving
evidence: "CALL continuously monitors these errors, enabling agents to detect when their world models are underperforming" (Sec. 3.3, Prediction-Accuracy-Driven Information Sharing)
method: CALL: each vehicle runs a DreamerV3-style RSSM world model; agents share latent state, hidden state and waypoint intentions; prediction error over last K steps widens communication range.
evaluation: CARLA Town04 trajectory planning, 150 and 230-250 vehicles; vs local-only, full-observation, latent-only and waypoint-only variants; prediction accuracy, bandwidth, return; one A100 per agent, no latency.
contribution: Ego-centric world models that exchange latent states and intentions raise multi-step prediction accuracy from 75/63/58% to 87/80/72% at 5/30/60 steps while sending about 0.11 MB instead of 5 MB.
flag: Predictive accuracy: DIRECT measure reported (Table 1: 5/30/60-step accuracy 75/63/58% without sharing vs 87/80/72% with CALL) plus downstream returns (about 100% gain over local-only, read from figures). Doubts: the paper does not define how prediction accuracy is computed; world model is per-agent ego-centric fed by other agents' latents, not one joint model; vehicle count is 230 in main text but 250 in App. E.1; bit arithmetic in appendix looks wrong (32 categorical x 32 classes stated as 60 bits); threshold c not found; real-time claims carry no inference latency figure; generative decoder used (not non-generative). Collision enters only as a reward term, no runtime interceptor. Last 14k characters (end of appendix) not read.

title: Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture for self-supervised pretraining on polymer molecular graphs
evidence: "JEPAs operate in an embedding space" (Sec. 1); context-subgraph embedding predicts target-subgraph embeddings of the same polymer graph (Sec. 2.2.2)
method: Polymer-JEPA: context and target wD-MPNN encoders with an MLP predictor; predicts embeddings of target subgraphs from a context subgraph of a static polymer graph; optional molecular-weight pseudolabel.
evaluation: Conjugated copolymer set (42966) electron-affinity regression and diblock phase classification at low label fractions; vs no pretraining, input-space SSL, random forest; R2, RMSE, AUPRC; no hardware.
contribution: JEPA-style subgraph embedding prediction for pretraining polymer graph encoders lifts electron-affinity R2 from 0.46 to 0.67 with 192 labels, but a fingerprint random forest still wins at the smallest sizes.
flag: E1 under the 2026-11-12 ruling: this is masked context-target latent prediction on a STATIC molecular graph - no future state, no dynamics, no agents. No direct measure of latent predictive accuracy either; only downstream property-prediction results (R2 0.46 +- 0.15 without pretraining vs 0.67 +- 0.01 best setting at 0.4% labels, RMSE 0.44 vs 0.34; AUPRC gain about 0.02-0.1 on diblock), so E2 would apply as a fallback. Most comparative values are only in figures. Paper is candid that a random forest on ECFP beats it at 0.4% and 0.8% labels and on the diblock task at all sizes. Text is inconsistent on whether pretraining helps up to 4% or 8% labels. Of interest only as a graph-JEPA architecture reference (non-generative latent prediction); the non-generative cell is ticked on that basis alone and can be dropped. No interceptor, no human takeover.

title: Transformer World Model for Sample Efficient Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
evidence: "Each agent is trained in isolation via a shared decentralized world model" (Sec. 3)
method: MATWM: STORM-style transformer world model with discrete categorical latents shared across agents, a teammate-action predictor, prioritized replay and action scaling; policies trained in imagination.
evaluation: SMAC 12 maps, PettingZoo Butterfly, MeltingPot at 50K-200K steps; vs MARIE, MAMBA, MBVD, QMIX, QPLEX, MAPPO, MAA2C; win rate and reward; ablations; 4 seeds; no hardware or timing.
contribution: A decentralised transformer world model with a teammate-action predictor reaches a 61.1% mean SMAC win rate within 50K-200K interactions, ahead of MARIE at 57.1% and MAMBA at 45.4%.
flag: ONLY DOWNSTREAM RESULTS: no direct measure of world-model predictive accuracy - losses are defined (reconstruction, reward, continuation, action mask, teammate, KL) but no prediction error, compounding error or teammate-prediction accuracy is reported; all results are win rates and returns, hence E2 per maintainer practice. Otherwise a clear (b) method paper with baselines and ablations (removing the teammate predictor drops 8m from 65.0 to 0.0 and so_many_baneling from 74.0 to 0.0). Multi-agent state is partial: the model predicts the focal agent's next latent plus other agents' action logits, not a joint latent state. Model is generative (decoder and reconstruction loss), so I did not tick non-generative inference. Possible inconsistency: 8m appears as 65.0 in Table 5 and 67.0 in Table 2 - check. Abstract's 'near-optimal in as few as 50K interactions' holds only on easy maps (hard maps use 200K; 3s_vs_4z 12.0). No hardware, training time or latency. Action-mask predictor acts only in imagination, not a runtime interceptor. No human takeover.

title: Graph World Model
evidence: World-model transition defined as s_{t+1} = f_tr(s_t, a_t) where f_tr "can be a neural network" (Sec. 2.2)
method: GWM: multi-modal graph state with action nodes; token (GWM-T) or embedding (GWM-E) message passing feeds a LoRA-tuned Llama-3-8B and Stable Diffusion decoder across six task families.
evaluation: Goodreads, Multi-Modal-Paper, Amazon, Cora, PubMed, HIV, AgentClinic, LongBench v2, ALFWorld; vs GNN, LLM and diffusion baselines; task accuracy/F1/CLIP scores; A6000 GPUs; 0.213 s per case.
contribution: Casts multi-modal graph tasks, RAG, planning and multi-agent collaboration as one graph world model decoded by an LLM and diffusion model, matching or beating domain baselines on several benchmarks.
flag: ICML 2025. E1 reasoning: despite the name and a formal transition definition, no dynamics are trained or evaluated - every task is a static graph task (node/link/graph classification, recommendation, matching, image generation, RAG, QA), so on reading the model is not predictive in the sense of (b). ONLY DOWNSTREAM RESULTS: no direct next-state prediction measure; if the maintainer accepts it as a world model it would still fall to E2. Closest thing to state prediction is ALFWorld planning (GWM-E BERT-Score F1 92.13 vs T5 FT 91.82) and image generation CLIP/DINOv2 (Multi-Modal-Paper GWM-E 59.84/26.03). Multi-agent task is AgentClinic diagnosis accuracy only (GWM-T 50.00 vs LLaMA FT 45.00; table rows garbled in my reading, apparently a very small test set). Claims of best performance are overstated: INSTRUCTG2I, CLIP FT and LLAGA each beat GWM on some columns. No seeds or variances. Inference 0.213 s per case is far from RQ1 budgets. No interceptor, no human takeover. I read the first 100000 of 102209 characters.

title: GALDS: A Graph-Autoencoder-based Latent Dynamics Surrogate model to predict neurite material transport
evidence: A Graph Neural ODE predicts the time derivative of the latent concentration on a global graph following the neurite tree connectivity (Methods, close paraphrase)
method: GALDS: graph autoencoders compress velocity and concentration fields of neurite trees to a latent graph; a graph neural ODE integrates latent dynamics to predict material transport.
evaluation: Eight unseen NeuroMorpho neuron geometries plus heterogeneous-kinetics pipes and subtrees; vs PGNN; mean and max relative error against IGA solver; inference 0.03-0.12 min per geometry.
contribution: A graph-autoencoder latent-dynamics surrogate predicts transport in neurite trees with 1.0-2.7% mean relative concentration error on unseen geometries, against 7.2-9.1% for a physics-informed GNN.
