contribution: Extends joint-embedding predictive pretraining to multi-vehicle cooperative perception: agents predict masked bird's-eye-view latents from fused neighbour features, reporting 99.2% latent reconstruction similarity and 94.5% mAP@0.5 on OPV2V.
flag: Include as (b) latent prediction over joint multi-agent state, with doubts. Predictive accuracy: a DIRECT measure is reported - reconstruction cosine similarity of predicted vs target latents, 99.2% OPV2V and 99.6% DAIR-V2X, vs MAE 94.3% and BEV-MAE 95.1% (Sec. IV-F, Table IV) - alongside downstream mAP. BUT the prediction is SPATIAL (masked-region completion within one frame), not temporal: there are no dynamics, no action conditioning, and the authors list temporal modelling as future work, so it is a representation-learning predictor, not a world model in the forward-dynamics sense; maintainer may prefer E1 on that ground. Internal inconsistencies: reconstruction similarity is 99.2% in one place and 96.5% for the same six-agent configuration elsewhere (Fig. 8 text), with '-1.9% versus the four-agent peak'; Table V text gives mAP@0.5 96.5% for grid spatial attention while the headline is 94.5%; DAIR-V2X 24.8% is '94.1% of CoBEVFlow' in Sec. IV-D but '94.1% of CoCa3D' in the conclusion (CoCa3D is 22.6%, which it exceeds); 'supervised-level performance of 98.2%' is undefined. The abstract's '85% annotation reduction' does not appear in the body, which instead says annotations are eliminated in pretraining (detection head still needs sparse labels). All tables (II-X) are images absent from the extracted text, so table values could not be checked beyond what the prose repeats. Near-perfect cosine similarity may partly reflect an easy target (EMA teacher), not verified. 78 ms latency is on V100-class GPUs, not edge hardware; packet-loss robustness (85.1% at 20%, 76.3% at 50%) is a perception result, not jitter-aware control. Perception only; no safety outcome.

title: MEKOR: Multimodal Internet of Things and Edge Intelligence for Smart Stadium Operational State Perception and Resource Optimization
evidence: "The resulting venue representation evolves through knowledge-constrained latent dynamics and supports receding-horizon control of HVAC, lighting, gate routing, staffing, and storage." (Sec. I Introduction)
method: MEKOR: edge tokenization of multimodal sensors, reliability-weighted dynamic hypergraph over stadium zones, physics-constrained action-conditioned latent dynamics, and penalty-based MPC with deadline fallback to cached plan or rule policy.
evaluation: MSSD-Bench replay (SportsMOT+NWPU-Crowd+BDG2, 10 zones, 1200 windows, 5 seeds); baselines LSTM, TCN, PatchTST, ST-GNN, Early Fusion, Graph-MPC, PPO; occupancy MAE 5.21, energy nMAE 8.63%; Jetson AGX Orin P95 53.9 ms.
contribution: Action-conditioned latent dynamics over a reliability-weighted dynamic hypergraph of stadium zones, driving constrained MPC on a Jetson AGX Orin; cuts occupancy forecast error from 6.42 to 5.21 on a synthetic replay benchmark.
flag: Include as (b): predictive model whose state is a (hyper)graph of zones - graph state, NOT multi-agent state (zones are not agents). Predictive accuracy: DIRECT measures are reported with baselines and ablations (Table II: occupancy MAE 5.21 vs Early Fusion 6.42 and ST-GNN 6.83; energy nMAE 8.63% vs 10.84%; risk F1 0.902 vs 0.859; horizons 15/30/60 min 4.35/4.86/5.71; cross-event Table III; ablations Tables VI-VII), plus downstream control results (energy 77.8%, peak 73.4%, safety violations 2.1% vs Graph-MPC 4.2%). All abstract numbers are found in the body. Main doubts: (1) the benchmark is SYNTHETIC - three unrelated public datasets stitched by a replay protocol; temperature, CO2, discomfort and all action-dependent outcomes are generated by the authors' own equations, and they say results are not field measurements; (2) control results are 'reported descriptively because independently verified per-seed controller logs are unavailable' - an unusual admission that should be read as unverified; no std on control tables; (3) results are uniformly monotone and tidy across every table, and the prose is heavily hedged in a way that reads as possibly machine-assisted; author's accepted version, not final typeset. Criterion (d) is weak: Jetson latency is measured (10/20/40 zones P95 53.9/92.6/171.8 ms, INT8 model 32.4 MB) but against a 900 s (15 min) coordination deadline, compute only, no end-to-end or deadline-miss rate. No runtime interceptor in the strict sense: safety is constraints inside the MPC; the fallback to a cached plan or rule policy triggers on a missed compute deadline, not on a predicted hazard, and 'local alarms' are mentioned but not evaluated. Operator alerts are mentioned, no human-handoff study. RQ5 capped at 2 per protocol.

title: Multi-Hypothesis Tracking in a Graph-Based World Model for Knowledge-Driven Active Perception
evidence: "A labeled property graph is used to model a tomato plant, which can be queried to create predictions of truss locations." (Abstract)
method: Symbolic labeled-property-graph world model (Apache TinkerPop/Gremlin) of one tomato plant; semantic association of detections with multi-hypothesis tracking as hypothesis vertices; active perception skill resolves hypotheses.
evaluation: ABB IRB1200 arm with RealSense L515 on mock-up plant; situations 1-3 quantitative (precision/recall gain, viewpoints, hypothesis correctness), situation 4 qualitative; no external baseline; no latency reported.
contribution: Represents prior knowledge of a tomato plant as a queryable property graph and tracks competing data-association hypotheses inside it to drive a single robot's active perception.
flag: Graph world model in the knowledge-representation sense only: hand-built symbolic graph database, no learned dynamics, no latent prediction, no forward model of state evolution; 'predictions' are queried prior truss positions. Single robot arm, no multi-agent state (sharing the WM with other robots is mentioned only as a possible benefit). No direct predictive-accuracy measure of a world model; results are detection precision/recall and hypothesis correctness (Table I and Fig. 9), whose numeric values are not present in the extracted text (table rendered as image), so I could not transcribe them. Only comparison is skill A alone vs skill A plus B. Not safety related.

title: MAPF-World: Action World Model for Multi-Agent Path Finding
evidence: Sec. III.C: "This auxiliary prediction loss encourages the shared representation of the backbone to capture local future interactions".
method: Decentralized transformer policy with a fast action head and a slow world head that autoregressively predicts each agent's next local observation and neighbours' action intentions over a 2-step horizon.
evaluation: Simulated MAPF on six map sets, 2-256 agents; baselines LaCAM*, PIBT, MAPF-GPT variants, LaGAT; SAPE, token and horizon ablations; intention-token accuracy 66-75%; 2.7M parameters, 1.8 GFLOPs; no millisecond latency.
contribution: A 2.7M-parameter action world model for multi-agent path finding that predicts neighbours' intentions and next observations before acting, improving success over larger imitation-learned solvers on out-of-distribution maps.
flag: Main success-rate and runtime results are in Figs. 5-7 only; I could not read numeric values for them, so headline comparisons against MAPF-GPT are unverified here. Predictive accuracy appears only in failure analysis: cost-to-go tokens 75% (unfinished agents) vs 83% (finished), intention tokens 66% vs 75%; no baseline predictor for those. Text-stated ablations: no SAPE costs 3-19% SR (6.6% mean); no cost-to-go tokens gives 7% SR vs 23% for MAPF-GPT-6M. ISR falls from 92% in open maps to 45% in narrow corridors. Compute is given as FLOPs, not wall-clock; simulation only, no robots; collisions defined but not counted; no shield or veto. State is tokenised egocentric observations of up to 13 neighbours, not a graph. Generative (autoregressive) so non-generative cell not credited; latency cell not credited because no time figures.

title: Imaginative World Modeling With Scene Graphs via VLM for Object Navigation
evidence: "World modeling and imagination module builds a global environmental representation with a hierarchical scene graph and leverages VLM to predict unseen parts, offering a more comprehensive environment state for target search." (Fig. 3 caption, Sec. III-A)
method: SGImagineNav: zero-shot object navigation that builds a hierarchical object-region-floor scene graph and prompts a VLM to complete unobserved regions of the graph; frontier chosen by exploitation and exploration gains.
evaluation: Habitat HM3D (2000 episodes) and HSSD (1248): SR 65.4% and 66.8% vs zero-shot and supervised baselines; module ablations on 400 episodes; scene-graph precision/recall with and without prediction; GO1 legged robot demo. No latency.
contribution: Zero-shot object-goal navigation that uses a VLM to complete unobserved parts of a hierarchical 3D scene graph, raising success rate to 65.4% on HM3D and 66.8% on HSSD.
flag: E1 under the 2026-11-12 static-graph ruling, by analogy: the 'imagination' is spatial completion of unobserved regions of a STATIC indoor scene (a tree-structured scene graph), not prediction of future state or dynamics; the authors themselves list as a limitation that it 'lacks sequential planning' and could be extended 'to predict environmental changes'. It is symbolic VLM completion, not latent prediction, and the agent is single (no multi-agent state). Maintainer should confirm the ruling extends from masked latent prediction to VLM graph completion. If he reads it as predictive: it DOES report a direct measure of prediction quality (scene-graph precision and recall with and without prediction, Tables III(a), IV, V; std 0.0513 of confidence across 3 repeated inferences) plus downstream SR/SPL/SoftSPL, with ablations, so E2 would not apply. Table contents are images and absent from the text file, so the precision/recall values and Table I/II rows could not be read; only numbers in prose were checked (65.4%, 66.8%, +12.4% over ImagineNav, +5.2% over SGM, oracle 72.25%, upper bound 88.84%). Abstract 65.4% and 66.8% are confirmed in Sec. IV-B. Ablation gains stated in the intro (6.75% and 2.75%) cannot be verified without Table II. Baseline numbers are quoted from other papers under a different success distance (1.0 m vs 0.1 m here). Real-world result is qualitative only.

title: StyleAD: Safe and Adaptive Trajectory Planning via Style-Aware World Models
evidence: "The proposed world model factorizes multi-agent uncertainty into continuous personality and discrete intention variables, enabling reactive and style-consistent multi-agent rollouts." (Sec. V Conclusions)
method: Autoregressive next-motion-token world model over all traffic agents with conditional-VAE latents (continuous personality, discrete intention); frozen as reactive simulator for IL-pretrained, RL (VD-GRPO) fine-tuned ego planner.
evaluation: nuPlan Test14-Hard, 32 rollouts of 8 s: Div 0.64, Mk 1.56, off-road 3.77%, O-O coll 0.46%, E-O coll 0.66% vs Nexus, Plan-R1; nuPlan-Style score 80.53/85.33 vs Plan-R1 79.08/84.84; 8 A100 GPUs.
contribution: Learns a style-conditioned autoregressive world model of surrounding traffic agents and uses it as a reactive simulator to fine-tune a driving planner, with rollout realism and closed-loop scores on nuPlan.
flag: Borderline, maintainer should decide. (b) is met in substance: predictive generative model over joint multi-agent state, with baselines (Nexus, Plan-R1 Top-5/Top-32) and ablations (Table V: w/o personality Div 0.06, w/o intention Div 0.38 and E-O coll 1.33%). BUT no direct predictive-accuracy measure against ground truth is reported (no ADE/FDE, likelihood or token accuracy); the world model is assessed only by rollout-behaviour statistics (diversity, kinematic smoothness Mk, off-road and collision rates of simulated agents) and by downstream planner scores, and the paper says it evaluates rollouts 'rather than selecting a single trajectory that best matches log-replay'. Under the ruling that downstream-only papers are E2 I recommend exclude-E2; if rollout realism statistics count as a predictive metric it would be an include with RQ5 capped at 2. Generative token model, so no non-generative cell. 'Safe' in the title is a planner reward term, not a runtime interceptor. Gains over Plan-R1 are small (+1.45, +0.49) and the paper itself states mean score gains have 95% CIs including zero. Text is the author's accepted preprint, not the final edited version; no latency or inference-time figure.

title: Toward World Model-Empowered Integrated Sensing, Communication, and Decision for Complex Unmanned Systems
evidence: Closely paraphrased (Sec. III-C): a hybrid latent state with deterministic h[t] and stochastic z[t] lets the model "simulate future trajectories" of candidate actions before physical execution.
method: Vision framework: RSSM-style latent world model unifying sensing, communication and decision for heterogeneous unmanned systems, with AoI/variance-triggered sensing and a multi-granularity knowledge graph.
evaluation: Case study: 5 UAVs tracking ground targets, Rayleigh fading; vs modular SCD, SCD without WM, edge LLM, deep RL; about 30% lower AoI; tracking RMSE; no hardware or latency.
contribution: A magazine-style vision of world-model-driven integrated sensing, communication and decision for multi-UAV systems, with a small five-UAV tracking case study showing lower age-of-information than a no-world-model variant.
flag: Title on arXiv reads 'Towards ...' vs record 'Toward ...' - same paper. Magazine vision/overview article with open challenges, not a full method paper; hence E3. If the maintainer treats the case study as an evaluation it still lacks a predictive-accuracy metric (only task metrics: about 30% AoI reduction with no absolute values; tracking RMSE 5.20 m for edge LLM at 4 dB and a 3.60 m gain over deep RL, SCD absolute RMSE not stated), so E2 would be the fallback. Simulator not named. Threshold-triggered sensing/transmission is event-triggered scheduling, not a safety veto, so (a) not met. Knowledge graph is updated from predictions; the world model does not predict graph state. Read via WebFetch summary in one pass.

title: Cooperative Multi-Cell Fluid Antenna Systems
evidence: "an RSSM-based World Model that learns the latent dynamics of the inter-cell interference environment to predict future states without real-time feedback" (Case Study, Architecture Implementation)
method: Distributed model-based MARL for multi-cell fluid antenna systems: each base station holds an RSSM latent world model and a pointerformer plus ZF/Gaussian policy trained in imagination; predict-then-act frame aggregation.
evaluation: Simulation, 4 BSs, 4 UEs per BS, 100 ports, 10 ms slots: transmission slots vs UEs (FAS about 40% fewer than fixed antennas at 6 UEs); UE-state prediction error rate vs horizon (Fig. 4b, figure only).
contribution: Proposes per-base-station RSSM latent world models within decentralised multi-agent RL so cells predict user and interference states several slots ahead and cut signalling overhead in fluid antenna networks.
flag: Borderline. IEEE Network magazine article: largely an architecture/vision piece with one thin case study. A direct predictive-accuracy measure IS reported (Fig. 4b, UE-state prediction error rate vs prediction steps for 3-6 UEs) but only as a figure; no numeric error values appear in the text, and there is no competing predictor baseline or world-model ablation, only sweeps over horizon and UE count. The other result is downstream (transmission time slots; the only number in text is 'approximately 40%' for FAS vs fixed antennas, which is an antenna comparison not a world-model one). Recommended E2 for failing the metric-plus-baseline minimum, not for being downstream-only; maintainer may prefer include as architecture evidence or E3 as magazine overview. World model is each BS's local latent state, not a joint or graph state (GNNs are mentioned only as an option). No training details, hardware or latency of inference; only a big-O complexity expression. Latent RSSM imagination tagged non-generative loosely; RSSM also reconstructs observations, check. Not safety related.

title: Satellite-Orchestrated Low-Altitude Wireless Networks for Communication-Computing Resource Management
evidence: "The case study uses lightweight prediction and WM abstractions so that paired differences reflect resource management rather than a particular estimator." (Simulation Setup)
method: Architecture framework: satellites do slow regional orchestration, UAV clusters fast execution; digital twin, demand-prediction maps, a 'world model' for state completion and reporting rhythm, hierarchical actor-critic MARL.
evaluation: Simulation, 3 regions, 80-240 users, 80 one-second slots, 10 seeds; hierarchical vs flat MARL, local greedy, static equal: penalized delay -2.47 to -5.45%, QoS +0.41 to +1.68 points vs flat MARL.
contribution: Outlines a satellite-orchestrated UAV network control loop combining a digital twin, demand prediction and hierarchical multi-agent RL, with a small simulation showing modest delay and QoS gains over flat MARL.
flag: Only downstream task results (penalized delay, QoS satisfaction, service-energy proxy 210-247 J); NO direct measure of world-model or predictor accuracy. The world model is not actually learned or evaluated: the paper states the case study uses 'lightweight prediction and WM abstractions' and prediction error is injected as unbiased noise with standard deviation 0.10. The WM here means state completion and freshness estimation for stale telemetry, not a latent predictive model over graph or joint agent state, so exclude-E1 is equally defensible. Article describes itself as 'primarily an architectural framework' (IEEE Network magazine, early-access version, pagination not final). Abstract numbers 2.47%-5.45% and 0.41-1.68 points are found in the body. A 'safeguard' and 'pre-execution safety checks' are mentioned in passing but are queue-stability heuristics, not an evaluated interceptor.

title: A Tiered Multimodal Memory and Event-Graph Architecture for Real-Time Agentic AI Systems
evidence: "The world model is not itself a learned machine learning model, but a continuously materialized software state" (Sec III-A)
method: Reference architecture: streaming perception emits events into a temporal event-graph store with hot/warm/cold memory tiers; an LLM agent applies threshold formulas for attention, storage placement and retrieval.
evaluation: No experiment. Latency budget composed from published component p95 ranges (LLM 150-400 ms, world-model update 5-30 ms); estimated end-to-end alert latency below 500 ms. No baseline run.
contribution: Reference architecture pairing a materialised event-graph store and tiered memory with an LLM agent for streaming multimodal monitoring; latency is estimated from published component figures, not measured.
flag: Not predictive: the paper itself says the 'world model' is not a learned model but a materialised state store (entity/event graph), with no prediction of future state. No predictive-accuracy measure and no downstream results either: Sec VII states evaluation uses 'published component-level benchmarks' rather than measurements, so E2 would apply equally. ABSTRACT CLAIMS NOT IN BODY: 'improving anomaly precision and lowering storage cost versus naive full-retention baselines' and reduced alert latency - no precision, storage-cost or baseline figure appears anywhere; Table I has latency ranges only, unsourced. Single author, no affiliation shown. Unresolved citation '[?]' in Sec IV. References look unreliable: [4] 'D. Ha and J. Schmidhuber, World Models Revisited, IEEE Access 2024' is not a paper I can vouch for, and [2] and [11] carry the same arXiv id 2306.08107 for different titles. Repeated phrase 'This proposed architecture define' suggests mechanical rewriting.

title: A Self-Aware Data Platform with Predictive Elasticity: Closed-Loop Autonomy for Elastic, Reliable, and Governed Analytics at Scale
evidence: "Rather than claiming end-to-end predictive performance, we present a controlled baseline evaluation of reactive autoscaling under burst load on a Kubernetes testbed." (Abstract)
method: Architecture blueprint for a self-aware data platform: event-graph 'world model' of workloads, resources, policies and actions; SLO/error-budget control loops; ML demand forecasting with warm pools; policy-gated, verified actions with rollback.
evaluation: Only reactive Kubernetes HPA measured: 3-node home-lab cluster, about 3 min synthetic burst, 1 to 10 replicas, P50 latency 1.80 s; proposed system not implemented; comparison table is illustrative ranges.
contribution: Sketches a governed closed-loop autonomy architecture for data platforms built on an event-graph state model and predictive elasticity, supported only by a home-lab measurement of reactive autoscaling.
flag: The proposed system is unevaluated: no world model, forecaster or policy gate is implemented or measured, so there is neither a predictive-accuracy measure nor downstream results for the method; the only experiment characterises the reactive HPA baseline. Section IX-C is explicitly titled 'Controlled Testbed Evaluation Design (Planned)' and Table I gives 'illustrative' industry ranges (e.g. 96-99% SLO adherence for the proposal) that are not measurements. The event graph is a provenance/knowledge graph, not a predictive latent model, and the setting is one platform controller, so exclude-E1 also applies. Policy gating, human approval for high blast radius and rollback are described as design (would be runtime interception, criterion a/e) but never built or tested, hence runtime_interceptor no. Single author listed as 'Independent Researcher/Industry Practitioner', regional conference; an unresolved cross-reference 'Table ??' appears in the results; prose is generic and repetitive, possibly machine-assisted.

title: Latent Probabilistic Dynamic Embedding Supervised Deep Networks With Graph-Guiding for Soft Sensing in Industrial Process
venue: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering
evidence: "a probabilistic dynamic model with graph-guiding based on the past and current latent features is constructed in the latent space of the supervised deep networks" (Abstract)
method: Stacked supervised autoencoder soft sensor whose latent features are regularised by a variational RNN predictor and a KL-based graph-guiding term over time-lagged samples; single joint optimizer.
evaluation: Debutanizer column and sulfur recovery unit datasets; vs PLS variants, SAE variants, cVAE, RNN, STA-LSTM, VRNN, SageFormer; three ablations; MAE, RMSE, R2 of the quality variable. No latency.
contribution: Soft sensor for industrial quality variables that embeds a variational recurrent latent predictor with a temporal graph regulariser, evaluated on debutanizer and sulfur-recovery benchmarks.
flag: No graph or multi-agent STATE: the 'graph' links time-lagged samples of one process time series (edge weights = KL distance between kernel-density estimates at t-i and t) and only regularises latent features; the modelled system is a single process unit with 7 inputs. Latent prediction is a training regulariser, and the reported metric is contemporaneous quality-variable regression error (MAE/RMSE/R2), not accuracy of predicting future state; latent-prediction accuracy itself is never measured. So: a direct accuracy measure of the soft-sensor output exists, but not of a world model over graph state. If the maintainer reads (b) loosely (any latent dynamics plus any graph) this becomes borderline. All result tables (II-V) are images and their values are absent from the extracted text, so no metric value could be verified; prose only says the method is best. Read abstract, intro, Sec. III-B/C, Case I and conclusion; skimmed Sec. II and Case II.

title: Phase-Guided Self-Supervised Latent Representation Learning for sEMG-Based Gait Decoding
evidence: "A GRU-based latent-dynamics predictor was therefore introduced to encourage temporally continuous and predictable low-complexity latent trajectories." (Sec II, Latent Dynamics Consistency Constraint)
method: Self-supervised sEMG encoder: CNN features, FiLM gait-phase conditioning, fixed anatomical graph convolution over 8 muscle channels, trained with reconstruction plus a GRU one-step latent-consistency loss.
evaluation: 36 participants, LOSO, frozen encoder plus MLP probe for knee angle; LSTM and TS-TCC baselines, three ablations; R2 0.93, RMSE 3.28 deg at 40% labels; public-set R2 0.88; no hardware or latency.
contribution: A phase-conditioned self-supervised encoder for surface EMG with an anatomical channel graph reaches knee-angle decoding R2 0.93 with 40% of labels, against 0.84 for a supervised LSTM.
flag: Not a world model: biosignal representation learning for one person, no actions, no agents. The graph is a fixed 8-node muscle-channel adjacency, not a system or multi-agent state. Latent prediction exists only as an auxiliary training loss (one-step GRU, Eq. 23); NO direct measure of its predictive accuracy is reported, only downstream knee-angle decoding (R2, RMSE) and a t-SNE plot, so E2 would also apply under the Pillar 2 ruling. Text is the IEEE early-access author version (header still says JOURNAL OF LATEX CLASS FILES). Abstract numbers R2 0.93 and 0.88 both found in the body; the 0.88 public-dataset figure has no baseline beside it. Dropping the latent-dynamics loss costs R2 0.93 to 0.85 (Table VI).

title: Multi-Agent Model-Based Reinforcement Learning for Decentralized Spectrum Sharing in Low-Altitude Economy
venue: IEEE Transactions on Cognitive Communications and Networking
evidence: "The world model then rolls the latent state forward and predicts the next latent observation" (Sec IV-B, Behavior Learning)
method: MAMBA-UAV: per-UAV RSSM world model (GRU, discrete latents, cross-agent attention block) trained centrally; PPO actors and centralized critic learn on 15-step imagined latent rollouts; decentralized execution.
evaluation: Simulated UAV spectrum sharing, 10-25 UAVs, 4-10 subchannels, 5 seeds; vs IQL, IPPO, QMIX, MAPPO and six heuristics; reward over 25% higher, over 45% fewer training steps; NVIDIA RTX A800; no latency.
contribution: A Dreamer-style multi-agent world model with cross-agent attention lets UAVs learn spectrum sharing from imagined rollouts, cutting real environment steps by about half in simulation.
flag: Meets (b) on mechanism (latent world model over joint multi-UAV state with cross-agent attention) but reports ONLY downstream task results (reward, training steps to target reward). The sole world-model evidence is Fig. 8, training-loss curves (reconstruction, reward, KL) for one scenario, with no held-out prediction error, no rollout-horizon error and no world-model baseline; recommending exclude-E2 for that reason per the maintainer's ruling. Closely follows MAMBA (Egorov and Shpilman 2022, cited as [20]); novelty is the application. Tables III-V are images and their numbers are not in the extracted text, so the 25% and 45-50% figures could only be checked against the prose (intro says about 50%, Sec V-B says more than 45%). GPU named as RTX A800, which is not a standard model name. Simulation only; no safety content; no runtime interceptor (expected).

title: Collaborative Task Offloading in Space Computing Power Network: A World Model-Based Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Approach
venue: IEEE Transactions on Cognitive Communications and Networking
evidence: "it models action-dependent transitions rather than only static feature encoding" (Sec III-B, Learning System Dynamics From Environment)
method: WM-MAPPO: Transformer world model trained offline with one-step latent MSE on global satellite-network state and joint action; H-step latent lookahead gives a future-context vector to an autoregressive MAPPO policy.
evaluation: Simulated LEO/GEO/SSO network, 311 active agents, 7 load levels; vs MAPPO, T-MAPPO, COMA, D3QN, Lyapunov, MINLP, heuristics; completion 0.727 vs 0.693, delay 10.65 vs 10.99 s; 14 ms inference on RTX 3090.
contribution: A Transformer latent world model over joint satellite-network state gives MAPPO agents a lookahead context for task offloading, raising completion ratio from 0.693 to 0.727 in a 311-agent simulation.
flag: Meets (b) on mechanism (latent transition model over the joint state of 311 satellite agents) but reports ONLY downstream task results (completion ratio, delay, energy). The world model itself gets one training-loss curve (Fig. 4) with no value, no held-out prediction error and no world-model baseline; Eq. 37 bounds return deviation by latent error but that error is never measured. Recommending exclude-E2 for that reason per the maintainer's ruling. INTERNAL INCONSISTENCY to check: Sec III-B defines an action-conditioned model z(t+1)=M(s_t,a_t) with H-step rollouts, while Sec III-C and Algorithm 1 describe the world model as a Transformer encoder mapping joint observations to z_t (no action input, no rollout, called an implicit world model), and execution needs z_t distributed centrally or inferred from local observation alone. Horizon H is never given. Epsilon-greedy exploration is stated for all agents including PPO. Gain over MAPPO is small (0.727 vs 0.693) with no confidence interval in the text. 14 ms for 311 agents within a 100 ms decision interval is a GPU server figure, not onboard. Simulation only; no safety content.

title: Topology-Adaptive World-Model DRL for AAV Data Collection With Incomplete Information
venue: IEEE Transactions on Cognitive Communications and Networking
evidence: "we conduct an open-loop latent prediction error analysis" (Sec V-F, Latent Prediction Error Analysis)
method: TDMPC2-G: TransformerConv plus Set Transformer graph encoder maps partially observed sensor-network graph to a latent; TD-MPC2 latent dynamics, reward and value heads; MPPI planning; exit-reachability action mask.
evaluation: Simulated single-AAV data collection on random WSN graphs, three prior levels, 100 episodes; vs TDMPC2-GCN, DreamerV3-G, SAC, TD3, lawn-mower, TSP; terminal AoI 10-14% lower; h-step latent error (Fig. 11); 36 ms per step on RTX 3090.
contribution: A decoder-free latent world model over a partially observed sensor-network graph plans a drone's data-collection path, cutting terminal age of information by 10-14% and staying stable on unseen topologies.
flag: Graph state yes (variable-size WSN graph), multi-agent no: a single AAV; multi-AAV is future work. This is the only record in the batch with a DIRECT measure of world-model predictive accuracy: open-loop h-step latent MSE over 30 episodes per prior level (Sec V-F, Eq. 38, Fig. 11). But it is weak evidence and the maintainer should rule: values appear only as a figure with no number in the text, it is reported for TDMPC2-G alone (no baseline or ablation on prediction error, e.g. not for the GCN variant or DreamerV3-G), and latent error against the model's own encoder is not a fixed scale (authors concede smaller error under minimal prior does not mean better understanding). If v1.6 needs the baseline on the predictive metric itself, this becomes E2. Baselines and ablations exist for downstream metrics only. Tables II and III are images, values not in extracted text. The exit action mask does override the planner's action at execution time, but it enforces a mission exit constraint, is applied to all RL baselines and is not evaluated as a safety mechanism, hence runtime_interceptor no. 36 ms per step on a desktop GPU exceeds the 15 ms target; 188 MB model, split inference is proposed but not tested. Section cross-references in the organisation paragraph are wrong (e.g. Section II-D3, IV-D2). No safety content.

title: Graph World Model for Energy-Efficient Hybrid Beamforming in LEO Satellite Networks
venue: IEEE Transactions on Green Communications and Networking
evidence: "The world model is a graph-conditioned, action-conditioned performance surrogate for user-wise rates and total power" (Sec III-B, Fig. 2 caption)
method: GWM-RA: heterogeneous attention GNN encodes satellite-user interference graph; MLP heads predict user rates and total power for a candidate precoding action; actor-critic trained on this one-step surrogate reward.
evaluation: Simulated 5-satellite LEO downlink, 20 seeds; vs WMMSE-EE, ZF-EE, GNN-MFRL, MLP-MFRL; EE 15.2 vs 14.0 Mbps/W; over 60% fewer interactions; 1.2 ms inference vs 1350 ms WMMSE on dual RTX 4090.
contribution: A graph neural surrogate that predicts rates and power for a candidate precoder lets a satellite beamforming policy reach target energy efficiency with over 60% fewer environment interactions.
flag: Reports ONLY downstream task results (energy efficiency, interactions to threshold, constraint-violation rates, inference time); no rate or power prediction error for the surrogate is given anywhere, so exclude-E2 per the maintainer's ruling. E1 is also arguable and the maintainer may prefer it: the authors state the model is a horizon-one reward/constraint surrogate, that it does not include a recurrent transition module or multi-step rollout, that the latent is not a prediction target, and that under i.i.d. block fading the action does not affect the next state; it predicts the immediate outcome of an action on a graph state, not future state. State is a satellite-user graph with one centralized policy, not multi-agent learning. World model is not used online. 1.2 ms is a server GPU figure and the authors say it is not an onboard estimate. QoS and power violation rates (0.8% and 0.5% vs 27.3% and 18.9% without penalties) are training-penalty effects, not a runtime safety mechanism. Tables III-V are images; numbers checked against prose only. Abstract claim of over 60% fewer interactions matches Sec IV-C (0.8e6 vs 2.2e6).

title: Video-Causal State Space Model (VCSSM) for Video Analysis
evidence: "VCSSM integrates a learned causal graph into a latent state-space dynamics model, enabling the explicit modeling of cause-and-effect relationships over time." (Abstract)
method: Variational latent state-space model over 64 latent factors whose transition is masked by a jointly learned sparse DAG; rollouts and latent interventions; classifier or decoder head on I3D features.
evaluation: Kinetics-700, HMDB-51, UCF-101, HAR, CoPhy; vs Transformer, LSTM, CNN, DAG-free SSM; many ablations; top-1 accuracy, CoPhy factual/counterfactual accuracy; 72 fps on 2x RTX-3090.
contribution: Latent state-space video model with a learned causal DAG over latent factors, reporting 76.8% factual and 70.5% counterfactual prediction accuracy on CoPhy versus 73.0% and 62.4% without the DAG.
flag: BORDERLINE (b). Predictive latent dynamics with a graph (learned DAG among 64 latent factors of ONE video, not entities or agents; no multi-agent state). Evidence is mostly DOWNSTREAM action-recognition accuracy (Kinetics-700 86.8%, HMDB-51 90.4%, UCF-101 98.0%, HAR 98.77%); the only direct predictive measure is CoPhy outcome prediction accuracy (factual 76.8%, counterfactual 70.5% vs DAG-free SSM 73.0%/62.4%), with no multi-step rollout error despite Theorem 4 bounding it. If CoPhy accuracy is not accepted as predictive accuracy this is E2. Doubts: nearly all tables are images, so only inline numbers could be checked; claim that a 5.4M-parameter head on I3D features beats InternVideo2-6B on Kinetics-700 is implausible and should be verified; conclusion says four benchmarks, abstract lists five; garbled sentence 'and we make neither claim' and a stray code-fence fragment in Sec. IV-B suggest unedited machine-assisted text; 72 fps excludes the I3D extractor. Extends an earlier letter by the same authors (ref [13]). Theory section (Sec. III-C onward) only skimmed.

title: Dream to Drive with Predictive Individual World Model
evidence: "the decoder has only two branches to predict future trajectories of ego and VDI" (Sec. III-B, Future Decoding)
method: DreamerV3-style RSSM with per-vehicle latent branches and self-attention over vehicles; decodes 2 s future trajectories of ego and the 5 nearest vehicles; actor-critic trained in imagination.
evaluation: INTERACTION intersection log-replay (I-SIM), 8 and 632 scenarios; vs DQN, PPO, SAC, DreamerV3; success 85.00/74.79%, collision 14.17/23.93%; ADE in Fig. 8 only; RTX 2080Ti training; no latency.
contribution: A latent world model with individual per-vehicle branches and interaction attention that predicts ego and neighbour trajectories, raising driving success over DreamerV3 on INTERACTION intersections.
flag: Direct predictive accuracy IS reported but only as a figure: ADE of ego and neighbour trajectories versus prediction horizon (Fig. 8), no numeric values in text or table and no FDE; the ADE is compared across horizons of the same model, not against a baseline predictor, so the v1.6 'accuracy metric AND baseline' test is met only loosely (baselines exist for downstream success: DreamerV3 40.00/55.98, IWM ablation 50.00/61.11, PIWM 85.00/74.79). Maintainer may judge this E2. Not a joint prediction of all agents: only ego plus 5 nearest vehicles are decoded. Other vehicles are log-replayed (non-reactive). Table I header is garbled in the PDF; column reading inferred from text. Collision rate remains 23.93% on unseen scenarios. No runtime interceptor (collision penalty in reward only), as expected for Pillar 2. Record id ends with a stray full stop, kept verbatim.

title: Modeling Interactions between Autonomous Agents in a Multi-Agent Self-Awareness Architecture
evidence: "Our experiments showed that this knowledge allows an agent to localize itself, and to predict the GSs, i.e., position and velocity, of the neighboring agent from the videos in a self-supervised way." (Sec. VIII Conclusion)
method: MASAA: coupled generalized-state hierarchical DBNs (world model from odometry clusters, CG-KVAE video perception) with a Markov jump particle filter predicting ego and neighbour vehicle states plus anomaly signals.
evaluation: Two-vehicle overtaking in CARLA (8 runs) and iCab, single-agent KITTI; RMSE drift 2.897% vs literature SLAM figures 3.693%, 4.07%, about 5%; RTX 3070 laptop; no latency reported.
contribution: A self-aware driving architecture learns coupled hierarchical dynamic Bayesian networks from odometry and video to predict the states of two interacting vehicles, reporting 2.897% RMSE drift.
flag: Direct predictive-accuracy measure IS reported (RMSE drift of predicted states, 2.897%, in abstract and Sec. VII-A), not only downstream results. Doubts: (1) multi-agent state is only TWO vehicles (relative distance vector in an overtaking task), so multi-agent is thin; (2) baselines are SLAM numbers quoted from other papers (DSV-SLAM 3.693%, UnDeepVO 4.07%, Li et al. about 5%) on KITTI single-agent sequences, while 2.897% is stated for two interacting agents - not a like-for-like comparison and not re-run; internal comparison is overtaking model vs following model (Table III); (3) the bodies of Tables I-III did not survive text extraction (IV is in supplementary), so I could not check per-experiment values; (4) the model is generative (VAE + DBN), not non-generative; (5) anomaly signals are shown only qualitatively (Fig. 8), no detection rate, and the Active First-Person (action) module is future work, so nothing is intercepted. Filter is described as estimation/localization as much as prediction - maintainer may judge it closer to SLAM than a world model.

title: Graph Neural ODE Digital Twins for Control-Oriented Reactor Thermal-Hydraulic Forecasting Under Partial Observability
evidence: "integrates the learned dynamics to produce multi-step forecasts and reconstructions of missing signals." (Sec. 1, Introduction)
method: Physics-informed message-passing GNN encoder, latent neural ODE and node-wise decoder over a 17-node plant graph; topology-guided initializer seeds 5 uninstrumented nodes; autoregressive temperature rollouts.
evaluation: Three-loop thermal-hydraulic testbed with SAM simulator data; initializer ablation; observed-node MAE 0.17 K at 10 s to 3.66 K at 300 s; 9.5 ms per simulated second on RTX 4090.
contribution: A graph neural ODE digital twin forecasts temperatures across a 17-node reactor thermal-hydraulic graph, including five unsensed nodes, about 100 times faster than real time on a single GPU.
flag: Graph state, not multi-agent (plant control volumes), so multi-agent cell not credited. No quantitative baseline against another model; only ablation is the initializer with vs without global context (Table 4, e.g. HX2 L3 MAE 2.559 to 0.559) - minimum-evaluation test passes only on that ablation. Experimental-hardware test is qualitative only; all numbers are on simulator data. Abstract R2 'up to 0.995' does not match Table 4 (up to 0.99996; HX values 0.990-0.995). Missing-node rollout MAE averages 0.54 K (10 s) to 2.18 K (300 s). Speedup 104.49x on GPU, 146.02x on 1 CPU thread (Threadripper 5995WX); workstation not edge, no jitter or deadline analysis, latency cell credited loosely. Dataset count unclear (700 series vs 1000+50 designs). Supervisory control is future work; no runtime gate. Read via WebFetch summary in one pass.

title: Digital Twin Meets World Model: Proactive Control for UAV Swarms in Low-Altitude Wireless Networks
venue: IEEE Transactions on Network Science and Engineering
evidence: "The model consists of a graph neural network (GNN)-based encoder that extracts relational mobility features, a latent transition model that captures action-conditioned mobility evolution, and a decoder that reconstructs UAV positions for multi-step rollout." (Sec. VI-A)
method: DT-WM-MPC: GNN-encoded latent world model rolls out UAV-swarm mobility under candidate joint actions; a digital twin completes network states and checks feasibility; sampling MPC executes the best feasible first action.
evaluation: Simulated 4-16 UAV swarms, 200 m area; WM open-loop RMSE under 0.03 m (1-step), under 0.09 m (10-step); baselines MPC-DT oracle, Myopic-RS, Greedy, Random; planning 0.31-0.83 s vs 1.12-3.11 s.
contribution: A GNN-based latent world model predicts UAV-swarm mobility inside a digital-twin-verified MPC loop, with 10-step position RMSE under 0.09 m and 72-74% lower planning latency than full-twin MPC.
flag: Direct predictive-accuracy measure IS reported: open-loop rollout RMSE of predicted UAV positions against the digital twin (Sec. VIII-B/C, Figs. 4-5), plus downstream completion ratio and utility. Doubts: (1) no competing PREDICTOR baseline or WM ablation - accuracy is reported for the proposed WM alone; the baselines are controllers (MPC-DT oracle, Myopic-RS, Greedy, Random), so whether the v1.6 'baseline or ablation' test is met for criterion (b) is a judgment call; (2) ground truth is the authors' own simulator, numbers are read off figures ('approximately'), no tables, no hardware stated; (3) latent transition is a per-node MLP 'without additional message passing', so graph structure enters only through the encoder; decoder is reconstructive; (4) latency is 0.31-0.83 s per decision, far from sub-15 ms; latency is a cost metric, not a deadline constraint; (5) DT feasibility check filters candidate sequences inside the planner before selection - I scored this as a planner constraint, not a runtime interceptor; no collision or violation rate is reported despite the abstract saying 'safe'; (6) task-completion ratios are very low (10.6% vs 7.2% at U=4). Abstract claims (72-74% latency reduction, stable across scales) are found in the body.

title: Distributed World Model Enhanced Mixture of Experts for Resource Allocation in Space-Air-Ground-Sea Integrated Networks
venue: IEEE Transactions on Network Science and Engineering
evidence: "we construct an independent world model for each agent u in U based on the RSSM architecture" (Sec. V-A); "there is no shared coordination layer; each agent must infer the necessary environmental dynamics from its own history of local observations" (Sec. V-C)
method: DWM-MoE: each satellite, UAV and base-station agent trains its own RSSM world model on its own observations and a Top-k sparse mixture-of-experts policy with imagination-augmented PPO.
evaluation: Simulated maritime network (20 users, 2 UAVs, 2 BSs, 1 LEO); ablations without world model and without MoE; latent MSE 0.00946 (H=1) to 0.03111 (H=10); success rate, AoI, energy; no hardware.
contribution: Decentralised model-based MARL for maritime space-air-ground-sea resource allocation in which every agent keeps an independent RSSM world model and a sparse mixture-of-experts policy.
flag: BORDERLINE E1, maintainer should decide. Reason for E1: the world model is NOT over a graph or joint multi-agent state - each agent has an independent RSSM over its own observation, with no shared or relational model (Sec. V-A, V-C). What could flip it to include: the setting is multi-agent, and the LEO satellite agent's observation is global ('distribution of maritime users, network-wide task queue statuses, and global topology'), so that one agent's model does cover network-wide state. Predictive accuracy: a direct measure IS reported (Sec. VI-D, Fig. 7: latent MSE 0.00946/0.02292/0.03111 and cosine 0.9713/0.9320/0.9091 at H=1/5/10), so this is not an E2-downstream-only case; but it is latent-space error against the model's own encoder, with no predictor baseline. Other doubts: abstract says it 'outperforms state-of-the-art baselines' but the only baselines I found are the authors' own ablations (no world model; non-MoE) - no named external algorithm; gains quoted (14% AoI, 9.5% success, 3% energy) are read from figures; success rates differ between sections for nominally the same default (69.3% vs 66.7%). Text is the accepted author version ('not been fully edited'). No safety content.

title: RoadPowerFM: Graphormer-JEPA-Based Foundation Model for Road-Power Coupling Network
evidence: "The pretraining of RPFM involves partitioning the input graph into subgraphs (communities) and predicting the representation of a randomly selected target community based on a single context community." (Sec. III-A)
method: RoadPowerFM: Graphormer encoders pretrained with a JEPA objective that predicts target-community embeddings from a context community on road-plus-charging-station graphs, then LoRA fine-tuned for forecasting and siting tasks.
evaluation: Shenzhen EV-station load and road-speed forecasting, Seattle siting; GRU, LSTM, T-GCN, STGAT, GCN, GAT, GraphSAGE with and without RPFM; STGAT RMSE 138.89 to 122.55, zero-shot F1 0.7938; 32GB GPU.
contribution: A Graphormer-JEPA foundation model for road-power coupling networks predicts community embeddings in latent space and improves load and traffic forecasters when added to GRU, LSTM, T-GCN and STGAT.
flag: Predictive accuracy: reported only for the forecasters that USE the pretrained encoder (RMSE, MAE, accuracy for EV-station load and road-speed forecasting, each baseline with vs without RPFM); the JEPA latent prediction error itself is never reported. I counted the forecasting RMSE as a direct predictive-accuracy metric with ablation-style baselines, but the maintainer may see it as downstream. Bigger doubt on criterion (b): the JEPA predicts SPATIAL embeddings of masked graph communities on a static graph - it is graph representation pretraining, not a dynamics/world model, and there are no agents; if (b) requires temporal prediction of state, this is E1. Other checks: the abstract's 'average of 7.53%' appears nowhere in the body (body gives 9.38%, 11.48%, 10.30%, 12.42%, 7.33%, 8.44%, 9.70%); Sec. IV-A says the siting task uses San Francisco, Sec. IV-E says Seattle; load dataset is private and tiny (8 stations, 3 days); 102M parameters pretrained in 'approximately 15 mins'; GraphSAGE+RPFM precision 1.0000; Tables II-VI bodies did not survive text extraction so most numbers could not be checked. No latency figures, no safety content.

title: Model-Based Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Joint Port and Precoding Optimization in Multi-Cell Fluid Antenna System
evidence: "Using a world model, each BS can predict its future observations, enabling it to perform multi-step decision-making based on the current state" (Abstract)
method: Model-based MARL for multi-cell fluid antennas: each base station runs a GRU-based RSSM predicting its observations, with QMix-style aggregation of predicted rewards, and a Pointerformer policy for port selection and precoding.
evaluation: Simulated multi-cell network, 3-6 users, 10x10 ports; metric is transmission steps vs activated ports, users and prediction steps; only comparison is fixed antenna; no hardware or latency.
contribution: Each base station in a multi-cell fluid-antenna network uses an RSSM world model to act for several steps without fresh observations, cutting transmission time relative to fixed antennas in simulation.
flag: E2 under the maintainer's ruling: ONLY downstream task results are reported (transmission steps in Figs. 4-5); there is NO direct measure of the world model's predictive accuracy - 'accumulation of prediction errors' is asserted, never quantified. Also no model-free or other learning baseline and no ablation: the only comparison is fluid vs fixed antenna, which tests the antenna, not the world model. Evaluation is two figures in one paragraph of a short conference paper; values are read from plots ('over 50%', 'at least 20%'). Multi-agent state is weak too: each BS is an independent agent modelling its local observation; only the reward and termination predictions are aggregated across agents (Eq. 15-16). Minor inconsistency: setup says K = 4 users while Fig. 4 uses 3 and Fig. 5 uses 3-6. No safety content.

title: Learning to simulate realistic limit order book markets from data as a World Agent
venue: Proceedings of the Third ACM International Conference on AI in Finance
evidence: Sec. 4.2: "we unroll the model during training: we generate k steps ahead, feeding the model with the previous generated market states".
method: A single world agent replaces the trader population: an explicit parametric mixture or a conditional WGAN-GP generates the next order from aggregate limit-order-book features, inside the ABIDES simulator.
evaluation: NASDAQ ITCH data, four stocks, 3-4 training days and 9 test days; baselines prior CGAN, hand-calibrated multi-agent configuration; stylised-fact realism mostly in figures; no predictive error, no hardware or latency.
contribution: A generative world-agent simulator that learns to emit realistic limit-order-book order flow from market data, covering market, limit, cancel and replace orders, as an alternative to hand-calibrated multi-agent simulation.
flag: The model is predictive in the generative sense, but its state is aggregate order-book features (volume and order-sign imbalance, spread, returns); it deliberately collapses all traders into one world agent, so there is no graph and no per-agent or joint multi-agent state. If the maintainer treats a market as multi-agent state, it would then fail minimum evaluation (E2): no predictive-accuracy or distributional-distance number, comparisons are qualitative plots. Few numbers in text: median time to first fill under 50 s; mid-price impact about 0.5% and over 1% for two participation rates over 25 runs. Logical/finance domain only.

title: AGODE: Adaptive Graph ODE for Grid-free Fluid Modeling and Domain Adaptation
venue: Proceedings of the ACM SIGKDD International Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining
evidence: "AGODE employs graph neural networks to encode unstructured point cloud data into latent dynamics governed by neural ODEs" (Abstract)
method: GNN encoder maps fluid sample points to latent node embeddings; a context-conditioned graph neural ODE evolves them; noise perturbation plus mutual-information contrastive term gives multiple trajectories; decoder returns physical fields.
evaluation: Five fluid benchmarks (Prometheus, Navier-Stokes, Spherical-SWE, 3D Reaction-Diffusion, ERA5), in-domain and OOD; 11 baselines; MSE; four-way ablation; training on one NVIDIA A100; no inference latency.
contribution: A continuous-time graph neural ODE with parameter conditioning predicts fluid fields on unstructured points, reaching MSE 0.0302/0.0312 (in-domain/OOD) on Prometheus against 0.0323/0.0328 for the best baseline.
flag: Direct predictive accuracy IS reported (MSE vs ground truth, Tables 2-4, 11 baselines, ablation), so the (b) minimum evaluation is met. Borderline on topic: the graph is a neighbourhood graph over fluid sample points, not agents or an acting system, with no actions, safety or multi-agent content; include only if a latent predictor over graph state alone suffices, otherwise E1. The abstract and conclusion claim a 41% improvement in 95% confidence interval coverage but no table, figure or number in the body supports it. Navier-Stokes and 3D Reaction-Diffusion show lower OOD than in-domain MSE (0.0712 vs 0.0734; 0.0112 vs 0.0113) without explanation. The Table 2 caption says 10 baseline models but 11 baseline rows are listed. No standard deviations or seeds reported; margins over PURE are small. No latency or edge figures.

title: IoT-Brain: Grounding LLMs for Semantic-Spatial Sensor Scheduling
venue: Proceedings of the 2025 ACM Workshop on Access Networks with Artificial Intelligence
evidence: Sec. 4.3: the verifier "prunes contradictions, and resolves ambiguities until the graph is verifiably consistent with W".
method: LLM planners hypothesise a spatial trajectory graph for a sensing query; a grounding verifier checks it against a deterministic geometric campus model before a set-cover solver schedules cameras.
evaluation: TopoSense-Bench, 5250 queries, 2510 cameras; baselines hierarchical, reactive, backtracking planners; hybrid-task success 46.1% vs 6.2%; real testbed task completion 49.84%, latency 413.69 s; two A100 GPUs.
contribution: An LLM sensor-scheduling system that verifies hypothesised spatial plans against a campus digital twin before committing, raising hybrid-task success to 46.1% against 6.2% for hierarchical planning.
flag: Not a predictive world model: W is a static, explicit geometric and sensor-coverage map queried by tools, nothing is learned or rolled forward (only a Kalman ETA filter predicts arrival times). Graph state yes, the LLM modules are a pipeline rather than interacting agents. The verify-before-commit gate is why runtime_interceptor is yes, but it checks plan feasibility, not safety, and no safety metric is reported, so (a) is not met either. Latencies are hundreds of seconds. Naive Parallel beats it on completion (65.64% vs 49.84%). Whether the stated 37.6% gap over Backtracking is points or relative is unclear. Optional interactive user clarification mode exists but is not evaluated.

title: MultiWorld: A Multi-View World Model with Spatiotemporally Synchronized Interaction
venue: Proceedings of the 34th ACM International Conference on Multimedia
evidence: "Given that these methods are inherently single-view world models, we establish a specific protocol to ensure a fair comparison" (Sec 4.2)
method: Camera-controlled autoregressive video diffusion model generating several synchronized views: multi-view tokens flattened into one attention sequence, View-Aware RoPE phase shift, causal multi-view mask and parallel per-view KV cache.
evaluation: 20 images x 20 camera trajectories; baselines GameCraft, Matrix-Game, YUME run twice; VBench quality, RoMa matched pixels (18.76K vs 11.87K), user study, ablation; latency 23 s for 2 views.
contribution: A multi-view video world model that generates synchronized camera views with unified sequence attention, improving cross-view matched pixels to 18.76K against 11.87K for the best single-view baseline.
flag: Generative video model; the multi-user or multi-agent setting is nominal: the only per-view input is a camera trajectory, there is no agent state, no interaction between agents and no graph. No direct measure of predictive accuracy against ground-truth futures is reported: metrics are VBench perceptual scores, cross-view matched pixels between the model's own outputs, and a user study, so it would also fail the (b) minimum evaluation (E2) if E1 is not accepted. Pixel-space generative, so not non-generative inference. Low-latency is claimed but the measured end-to-end latency is 23 s (2 views), 37 s (3), 55 s (4); hardware for the latency figure is not stated (training used NVIDIA H20 GPUs). Table 2 ablation quality numbers (e.g. imaging quality 78.97) differ from Table 1 (63.40) with no explanation of the different setup. Further ablations are deferred to supplementary material not in this file.

title: From State Reconstruction to State Interpretation: S2VMO, an Agentic Voxel-Based Digital Twin for Space Habitat Structural Monitoring
venue: Proceedings of the Special Interest Group on Computer Graphics and Interactive Techniques Conference Posters
evidence: "the absence of experimental validation add to the limitation of this methodology" (Sec 5 Discussion)
method: Two-stage neural surrogate reconstructs strain and stress fields from four strain sensors onto a 12,873-node voxel graph in Neo4j; GraphRAG LLM agents answer structural queries and give advisory inspection recommendations.
evaluation: Single simulated dome-shaped steel truss with FEM training data; only descriptive stress statistics (mean about 0.07 MPa); no baseline, ablation, accuracy metric, latency or hardware.
contribution: A three-page poster describing a voxel-graph digital twin of a space habitat truss that LLM agents query for anomaly attention, diagnosis and advisory inspection recommendations.
flag: Three-page SIGGRAPH poster, pilot framework with no evaluation: no reconstruction error, no agent answer accuracy, no baseline or ablation, and the authors state there is no experimental validation. No direct predictive accuracy measure and no downstream results either. It is also off-topic on reading (E1 would equally apply): the so-called voxel world model is a static state reconstruction store, not a predictive model of future state, and the multi-agent wording refers to LLM query agents, not a modelled joint agent state. Outputs are advisory to human operators but no handoff is studied. Reconstruction pipeline and case study are reused from an earlier ASCE Earth and Space 2026 paper by the same authors (cited as to appear).

title: Hierarchical Belief Modeling for Zero-Shot Opponent Adaptation in Partially Observable Multi-Agent Navigation
venue: Proceedings of the 3rd International Conference on Computer Application and Computer Graphics
evidence: Sec. 4.7: "a world-model loss regressing the next-frame rasterized tensor" (auxiliary loss only).
method: HORIZON RL agent: equivariant spatial backbone, fast/slow recurrent belief encoder, relic-centric graph attention, information-gain reward, opponent-conditioned policy mixture; next-frame world-model loss is auxiliary.
evaluation: Lux AI Season 3, 500 best-of-five episodes; baselines RuleBot, FlatPPO, IMPALA-LSTM, RL2; five component ablations; match win rate 0.72 vs 0.64 best baseline, TrueSkill 29.1; no latency.
contribution: A hierarchical belief-encoding RL agent for a partially observable two-team game that adapts to unseen opponents, improving match win rate from 0.64 to 0.72 over a recurrent meta-RL baseline.
flag: Judgment call between E1 and E2. Beliefs (Bernoulli over relic tiles, posterior over hidden game parameters, opponent-type classifier) and a next-frame loss exist, but the world model is an auxiliary training loss never used for prediction at runtime, is not ablated on its own, and no prediction accuracy is reported for any of them; the paper is about win rate in a competitive game. If the maintainer counts the belief encoder as latent prediction over multi-agent state, it still lacks a predictive metric (E2). No seeds, variance or unit count per team reported. Text claims removing RC-GAT gives the largest MWR drop but Table 2 shows w/o DMBE lower (0.63 vs 0.65). Episode win rate 0.77, adaptation gain +0.16.

title: Symbolic-JEPA: Where Symbolic AI Meets Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture for NL–FOL Conversion
evidence: "we propose Symbolic-JEPA, a neuro-symbolic predictive representation model that unifies semantic and logical learning within a single framework" (Abstract)
method: JEPA-style pretraining for NL-to-FOL translation: AMR and FOL parse graphs merged into one scaffold, T5-base encoders with structure-guided attention, EMA target encoder, masked-component embedding prediction, then fine-tuned decoder.
evaluation: ParaLogic (9,344 paragraph pairs) and MALLS; baselines fine-tuned T5, Gemini zero-shot, Text-JEPA; well-formedness, predicate similarity, logical equivalence, conversion score (0.6985, 0.9015); ablations; one NVIDIA A100; test inference about 2 minutes.
contribution: A JEPA-style neuro-symbolic encoder that predicts masked components of joint language and logic parse graphs, raising paragraph-level NL-to-FOL conversion score to 0.6985 against 0.5570 for Text-JEPA.
flag: On reading this is semantic parsing (natural language to first-order logic), not a world model: the JEPA predictor reconstructs embeddings of masked tokens in a static sentence parse graph; there is no dynamics, no future state, no agents and no acting system. It matches (b) only on the literal words latent prediction over a graph, so I recommend E1; if the maintainer reads (b) literally, note that no direct measure of latent-prediction accuracy is reported, only downstream translation metrics (SWF, PSE, LE, CS), which would make it E2. Inconsistencies: experimental text names Gemini-2.5-Flash as baseline but Table 3 lists Gemini-2.0-flash; under the frozen-encoder ablation (Table 10) the CPP-only and LDP-only decoders score higher CS (0.6367, 0.6465) than the full setup (0.6220). Long file (225k chars): I read abstract, introduction, method overview and predictor sections, experimental setup, Table 3, limitations and ablation Table 10; I did not read the dataset-construction section, appendix walkthroughs, prompts or worked examples in full.

title: Rethinking the Reliability of Multi-agent Systems: A Perspective from Byzantine Fault Tolerance
venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
evidence: "treats all agents equally regardless of their reliability" (Confidence-Guided Byzantine Consensus Protocol, on classical BFT voting that CP-WBFT replaces with confidence-weighted voting; no world model or future-state prediction anywhere in the paper).
method: CP-WBFT: confidence-probe weighted Byzantine consensus for LLM multi-agent systems; verbalised (PCP) or hidden-state logistic-regression (HCP) confidence; agents adopt higher-confidence neighbour answers, then confidence-weighted vote.
evaluation: GSM8K, XSTest, CommonsenseQA (10 questions each); 7 topologies; 7 nodes with 6 Byzantine, 15 with 14; PCP vs HCP; final answer accuracy; no hardware or latency.
contribution: Confidence-weighted Byzantine consensus lets LLM multi-agent systems reach correct answers with up to 6 of 7 agents faulty on complete and star topologies, using hidden-state confidence probes.
flag: Pillar 2 / criterion (b) NOT met: no predictive world model, no latent prediction of future state; the HCP probe is a per-response correctness classifier on one agent's hidden states (probe test accuracy 84-95 percent, AUC 0.91-0.98 on GSM8K/XSTest - that is classifier accuracy, not world-model predictive accuracy). Outcomes are downstream answer accuracy only (HCP FAA 100 on complete and star-leaf, 57.14 on random/layered/tree, 42.86 chain, 28.57 star-centre; PCP 68.57-100 GSM8K, 4.29-42.86 XSTest). Maintainer may want to consider criterion (c) instead (robustness of LLM multi-agent systems to malicious agents, with XSTest as a safety set), but the metric is accuracy not a hazard/violation rate, and consensus replacing an agent's answer is not a veto/halt, so I did not credit (a) or (c). Doubts: only 10 questions per dataset; only experimental baseline is PCP vs HCP plus a pilot with traditional agents (PBFT etc. discussed, not run); text says traditional agents collapse to RA=0 percent but Table 1 lists RA 100 percent; honest and Byzantine agents are different models (LLaMA3.1 vs LLaMA3; GPT-4o-mini vs GPT-3.5), so the comparison is not fully controlled. Record title says Systems, paper says System - same paper. Read via one WebFetch pass of the PDF (summarised), not page by page.

title: Predictive Auxiliary Learning for Belief-based Multi-Agent Systems
evidence: "Each point corresponds to a single training episode, where belief accuracy is measured by the decoder loss and performance is measured by the average number of steps required to capture the prey." (Experiments, Correlation between Belief Accuracy and Performance)
method: BEPAL: decentralised communicating MARL agents with an LSTM belief state; a training-only decoder predicts other agents' positions, identities, motion and next actions (vector and grid targets) as an auxiliary MSE loss.
evaluation: Predator-Prey, Traffic Junction, Google Research Football 3v1, RWARE vs TarMAC and MAGIC: steps 17.65 vs 39.15, TJ success 0.83 vs 0.66, GRF 0.86 vs 0.31; belief-error vs performance correlations. No hardware or latency.
contribution: Auxiliary belief-prediction training for communicating multi-agent RL: a training-only decoder forces each agent's hidden state to predict global multi-agent state and motion, improving task performance over TarMAC and MAGIC on four benchmarks.
flag: BORDERLINE E2 vs include - maintainer should decide. Predictive accuracy of the belief model is MEASURED (decoder MSE loss) but never REPORTED as a value or compared with a baseline: it appears only as a scatter plot (Fig. 5, PP) and as correlations with task performance (Table 2: Pearson -0.25/-0.36/-0.40, Spearman -0.54/-0.86/-0.94 for TJ hard, TJ add-rate 0.1, GRF). All headline results are downstream (steps to capture, success rate, RWARE reward 14.11 vs 0.04), hence E2 under the maintainer's ruling; if a correlation between prediction error and return is accepted as a predictive-accuracy metric it would be includable under (b) with multi-agent state clearly satisfied. Also check how predictive it is: most targets are estimation of the CURRENT unobserved global state (positions, identities, explored area, obstacles); the forward-looking part is motion direction and, in TJ only, each car's next action - no multi-step rollout. Text calls the correlation 'strong' although Pearson is -0.25 to -0.40. TarMAC and MAGIC serve as the no-auxiliary-loss ablation but differ in architecture, so the gain is not cleanly attributed. Number of seeds not stated; auxiliary weights not given. Transfer table (PP, 19.76 vs 18.23, 22.41 vs 22.41, 54.62 vs 55.23 steps) is same-task layout transfer, not hazard composition. AAAI Spring Symposium paper, 9 pages; abstract has no numbers to verify. Traffic Junction involves collisions but no collision rate is reported, so (c) is not met.

title: On Sample-Efficient Generalized Planning via Learned Transition Models
evidence: Abstract: "a neural model explicitly approximates the successor-state function"; states are instance learning graphs embedded with k=2 Weisfeiler-Leman iterations (Appendix E).
method: LSTM or XGBoost predicts the successor-state WL graph embedding (direct or residual delta); a symbolic layer matches the prediction to the nearest valid successor and emits its action.
evaluation: Four IPC domains (Blocksworld, Gripper, Logistics, VisitAll), interpolation/extrapolation splits; baselines Plansformer, PlanGPT, SymT, Fast Downward; metric plan success rate; H100 GPU, about 1 GPU-hour, no latency.
contribution: Learns compact successor-state models over Weisfeiler-Leman graph embeddings for generalized planning, reaching 0.50 (Blocksworld) and 1.00 (VisitAll) extrapolation success with about 1M parameters against far larger transformer planners.
flag: Predictive accuracy: NOT reported - only downstream plan success/coverage (extrapolation: Blocksworld WL-XGB delta 0.50 vs SymT 0.13; VisitAll 1.00 vs 0.64; Gripper 0.42 vs SymT 0.79; Logistics 0.00 for all learned models); no next-state or embedding error, hence E2 under the maintainer's ruling. Model is predictive with a relational graph state (single-agent classical planning, no multi-agent). Symbolic successor matching constrains outputs to valid actions but is a decoder, not a safety interceptor. Internal inconsistency: Gripper WL-LSTM state extrapolation given as 0.42 in one place and 0.25 in another. Table 1 interpolation values could not be parsed reliably from the PDF text. Small test sets (e.g. 20 Blocksworld extrapolation instances). ICAPS short paper, arXiv is the extended version.

title: PLM-based World Models for Text-based Games
venue: Proceedings of the 2022 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing, EMNLP 2022
evidence: "We show that our model improves future valid action prediction and graph change prediction." (Abstract)
method: Two BART encoder-decoders predict next-step knowledge-graph difference and next valid actions from current observation, graph and action; template retrieval plus constrained template filling with hard negatives.
evaluation: JerichoWorld 2.0, 9 unseen test games; vs CALM, Worldformer-BART, +COMET filter; ablations; tuple-level EM/F1 for graph and actions; 3 seeds; RTX 3090 Ti, no latency.
contribution: Pre-trained-language-model world model for text games that predicts next knowledge-graph changes and valid actions zero-shot on unseen games, lifting action EM from 25.56 to 40.67.
flag: Direct predictive accuracy IS reported: next-step graph-difference EM/F1 41.87/42.53 vs Worldformer-BART 40.38/41.12 and action EM/F1 40.67/55.16 vs 25.56/37.51 (p<.001, 3 seeds), with ablations. Caveats: state is a knowledge graph of a SINGLE-agent text game, not multi-agent; prediction is generative token decoding (no latent/non-generative inference); the graph-prediction gain is small (+1.5 EM) and the headline gain is on valid-action prediction, which is closer to an affordance task than state prediction; graph task predicts additions only. Baseline Worldformer is the authors' BART re-implementation on their own regenerated dataset (JerichoWorld 2.0). Hardware line is in the appendix (3-5 hours per epoch); appendices otherwise not read.

title: DAVIS: Planning Agent with Knowledge Graph-Powered Inner Monologue
venue: EMNLP 2025 - 2025 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing, Findings of EMNLP 2025
evidence: DAVIS "estimates the transition and reward models using prior experiences retrieved from a TKG" (Sec. 3.3)
method: Single LLM agent whose world model is a temporal knowledge graph queried by inner monologue to predict next observation and reward; actor plans, critic compares predictions with outcomes and triggers replanning.
evaluation: ScienceWorld, 30 tasks, 90 test variations; vs SayCan, ReAct, Reflexion, RAP; mean score 65.06 (about 1.8x baselines); HotpotQA EM 56.25, F1 73.8; RTX 3060; about 43k tokens per action; no latency.
contribution: An LLM planning agent that uses a temporal knowledge graph as a world model to predict action outcomes before acting, improving ScienceWorld task scores over ReAct, Reflexion and RAP.
flag: ONLY downstream results: no direct measure of the world model's predictive accuracy (no transition or reward error, no match rate of predicted vs actual observations) - task scores, steps per replan and multi-hop QA EM/F1 only; hence exclude-E2 per the maintainer's practice. (b) is met only nominally: the state is a knowledge graph, predictions are prompted LLM reasoning over retrieved subgraphs, not a trained dynamics model; single agent. Not a runtime interceptor: the critic acts after execution to trigger replanning; an 'Alert supervisor' step and plan validation 'prior to execution' are mentioned but unspecified and untested. Paper says the world model 'consistently improves performance across all tasks' but its Table 1 shows Mix Paint 40.00 to 36.37; step limit stated as 80 and 100; DAVIS loses on Botany (26.83 vs about 40) and trails HOLMES/GraphRAG on QA; baselines reimplemented, SwiftSage dropped.

title: Semantic-based behavioral decision-making method for construction robots in worker-robot collaboration
venue: Proceedings of the International Symposium on Automation and Robotics in Construction
evidence: "If only one WRC state is matched, or if multiple WRC states are matched but mapped to the same behavior, that behavior will be the decision-making result." (Sec 3.3.2)
method: Worker-robot scene as a semantic multigraph; extended semantic event chain of states, behaviours and manual guard conditions extracted from VR demonstrations; robot picks behaviour by static and dynamic graph matching.
evaluation: VR wall-panel installation (Unity, ROS), one worker and one robot, 30 subjects. 18 of 20 demonstrated policies feasible; first-attempt success 16/18 (89%), 70% with 20 new subjects. No baseline.
contribution: Symbolic graph state model and learning-from-demonstration policy that lets a construction robot choose behaviours by matching partial observations to demonstrated worker-robot states, tested in VR panel installation.
flag: Not predictive: the 'semantic world model' is a hand-defined symbolic scene graph plus a demonstrated transition table used to RECOGNISE the current state by graph matching; nothing predicts future state and there is no latent. Only DOWNSTREAM results (policy feasibility and task success rates), no predictive-accuracy or state-matching accuracy figure, and no baseline or ablation, so E2 would also apply. The abstract's '90% success rate' is 18 of 20 policies from 10 subjects. Perception is perfect in VR (authors admit this); guard conditions are set manually; one worker and one robot only, so multi-agent state is minimal. Possible (a) angle that I did NOT credit: when candidate states map to different behaviours 'the default waiting behavior is adopted to avoid any risks' - an abstention rule, but it is part of the decision maker, not an interceptor, and no safety metric is reported.

title: CDD O-RAN: Causal Discovery-Driven Model-Based Planning for xApp Conflict Mitigation in O-RAN
venue: 2026 International Conference on Networking and Network Applications (NaNA)
evidence: "the masked predictor serves as the world model for the planner" (Sec III-B)
method: Offline causal dynamics learning recovers a sparse NCP-KPI causal graph; the frozen graph enumerates xApp conflicts and masks a probabilistic one-step world model used by QACM, CEM, MPPI, MCTS planners.
evaluation: Two synthetic near-RT RIC environments (4 and 5 xApps), OOD ranges; dense MLP world-model baseline; graph recovery F1 1.00; z-score utility, Cohen's d 0.35 and 1.79; no latency or hardware.
contribution: A causal-graph-masked world model of shared O-RAN control parameters and KPIs supports conflict enumeration among xApps and one-step planning, beating a dense MLP model on utility in two synthetic benchmarks.
flag: No direct measure of the world model's predictive accuracy is reported (no NLL, MSE or rollout error for CDL or the MLP): the comparison of world models rests only on downstream planner utility (Table I), so under the maintainer's ruling this is E2. The one direct model-quality measure is structural: causal graph recovery recall and F1 = 1.00 against ground truth, with no baseline discovery method; the maintainer may judge whether that counts as predictive accuracy, in which case it would be an include under (b). Evaluation is thin: two synthetic environments with closed-form Gaussian KPI functions, Neval = 30 steps, a single seed each for discovery and mitigation (authors admit more seeds are needed), planning horizon H = 1. The Env. I effect is small (d = 0.35) with overlapping standard deviations. Multi-agent only loosely: xApps appear as priority weights and KPI targets in the cost function, the state is the shared NCP-KPI vector. runtime_interceptor set to no: the planner picks a resolving parameter value rather than vetoing or halting an action, and the paper frames it as QoS conflict mitigation, not safety; arguable. No latency measured despite the 10 ms-1 s control-loop framing. Code on GitHub.

title: GraphPerf-RT: Graph-Driven Performance Modeling with Calibrated Uncertainty for OpenMP Scheduling on Heterogeneous Embedded SoCs
venue: International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence
evidence: "We use GraphPerf-RT as a deterministic transition model with epistemic uncertainty quantification" (Section 5.3, RL Baseline Evaluation)
method: Heterogeneous graph attention network over task, core and memory nodes with evidential (Normal-Inverse-Gamma) heads predicts makespan with uncertainty per scheduling action; shared world model for multi-agent Dyna-style RL.
evaluation: 73,920 runs, 42 benchmarks, Jetson TX2, Orin NX, RUBIK Pi; seven baselines: RMSE 0.45, R2 0.81, Spearman 0.95, PICP 99.9%; 2-7 ms on-device; RL makespan 0.97 s versus 2.85 s.
contribution: A heterogeneous graph surrogate predicts OpenMP makespan with evidential uncertainty in 2-7 ms on embedded ARM boards and serves as the shared world model for multi-agent model-based DVFS scheduling.
flag: DIRECT predictive-accuracy measure IS reported (Table 2: RMSE 0.45, MAE 0.24, R2 0.81, Spearman 0.95 on log makespan versus Linear, RF, MLP, GCN, HGT, HGT+Ensemble, HGT+MC Dropout; ablations in Table 1), plus downstream RL results, so the (b) minimum is met. Doubts: (1) it is a one-shot outcome regressor (graph, device, state, action -> makespan), not a next-state dynamics model; the paper calls it a 'transition model' but no next-state or thermal prediction accuracy is shown; maintainer should decide whether that counts as predictive for (b). (2) Multi-agent is per-core DVFS agents sharing the model; typical graph is tiny (8 nodes, 56 edges). (3) Runtime gate gate(a)=(Epi(a)<=eta) AND (PI(a)<=Tmax) filters candidate actions before execution, which is close to a veto, but it sits inside action selection and is never evaluated: all four RL methods, including model-free ones without it, show 0% thermal violations, so 'zero thermal violations' credits nothing; I set runtime_interceptor no. The gate also compares a makespan prediction interval with a temperature cap, which does not parse. (4) 'Calibrated' is generous: PICP 99.9% at nominal 95% and 98.1% at 80% means intervals are far too wide. (5) Abstract '66% and 82% versus model-free baselines' is versus SAMFRL only; single-agent model-based with the same model is WORSE than model-free (3.56 s versus 2.85 s). (6) Splits are stratified by benchmark, so no held-out-program generalisation; 2-7 ms has no stated device or deadline (latency breakdown is in supplement, not read); many details deferred to supplementary material. (d) considered but no explicit latency constraint is stated.

title: Learning to Deceive and Persuade: Predictive Agents with Language and Personality Diversity in Social Deduction Games
evidence: "The JEPA component takes the current latent state and a candidate action, predicts a next latent state" (Section 3.1, System Overview)
method: Each Werewolf agent encodes a latent belief; a JEPA MLP predicts the next latent per candidate action; planner heads choose talk, vote or kill; peer utterances shift beliefs.
